questions.text: A company with multiple accounts AWS organized in an OR in AWS Organizations needs to ensure that no member account can create resources outside the 'sa-east region-1', irrespective of the permissions of the IAM What is the correct approach??
options: Apply one Service Control Policy (SCP) in OR denying shares outside the permitted region using the condition key aws:RequiredRegion
Create a IAM Policy on each account restricting the Region
Use only resource tags to identify the Region
Request each team to manually configure the console for the correct Region
questions.explanation: SCPs the OU represent a limit of permissions that no policy of IAM within the member accounts may exceed; use the condition aws:RequestedRegion allows you to deny actions outside the desired Region in all OR accounts.

questions.text: A multi-tenant application in DynamoDB it needs to ensure that each end user can only access the items in the table that belong to him, identified by a partition key equal to his user ID. Which feature allows to apply this restriction directly to the user's temporary credentials?
options: IAM Policy with conditions based on policy variables (LeadingKeys) combined with Web Identity Federation
Use only Security Groups to restrict access
Create a table DynamoDB separate for each user
Allow full access to DynamoDB for all authenticated users
questions.explanation: Policy IAM with conditions such as dynamodb:LeadingKeys allow you to restrict a federated user access only to items whose partition key corresponds to your own identifier, a common pattern in multi-tenant applications.

questions.text: A company needs to expose a API private which should be accessible only from within your VPC, without going through the public internet. What configuration of Amazon API Gateway meets this requirement?
options: Expose the API directly via Elastic IP in an instance EC2
API Private Gateway, accessed via VPC Interface Endpoint (PrivateLink)
API Regional Gateway, publicly exposed
API Edge-Optimized Gateway
questions.explanation: Private APIs of API Gateway can only be accessed from a VPC by means of a VPC Interface Endpoint (AWS PrivateLink), keeping traffic out of the public internet.

questions.text: A critical application uses the Amazon Aurora and needs a RPO (Recovery Point Objective) close to zero and RTO (Recovery Time Objective) low in case of failure of an entire Region. Which configuration is most suitable?
options: Migratory to Amazon DynamoDB without changing the rest of the architecture
Monthly manual backup exported to the S3
Aurora with a single instance in an AZ and daily snapshots
Aurora Global Database, with secondary replicas in another region with low latency replication
questions.explanation: The Aurora Global Database replicates data between regions with latency typically below 1 second, allowing RPO close to zero and quick recovery (RTO low) in case of regional failure.

questions.text: A serverless architecture uses AWS Lambda integrated into one Amazon SQS Standard Queue. Consumers occasionally process the same message more than once, causing duplicate side effects. What is the explanation and best mitigation?
options: The problem is caused by Lambda, that always processes every message exactly 3 times
SQS Standard offers delivery 'at least once' (at-last-once); the application must be designed to be idempotent, or use a row FIFO with deduplication if order and uniqueness are critical
SQS Standard guarantees exactly-once delivery; the problem is in the consumer code, which must be fixed without changes in the queue
It is not possible to solve this problem with SQS; it is necessary to migrate Kinesis
questions.explanation: Rows SQS Standard deliver 'at-least-once', and can generate duplicate messages. The recommended solution is to make the processing idepotent or use a row FIFO with content deduplication when uniqueness is essential.

questions.text: A company uses Amazon S3 as the origin of CloudFront and it needs to ensure that even during a planned maintenance in primary origin, the requests are met by a secondary origin in another Region. CloudFront enable it?
options: Origin Failover with Origin Groups
Field-Level Encryption
Lambda@Edge for cache only
Signed URLs
questions.explanation: Origin Groups no CloudFront allow setting up a primary and secondary source; in case of faults (configurable error codes), CloudFront automatically fails to cause secondary origin.

questions.text: A video processing application needs storage of extremely high throughput and low latency shared between hundreds of instances EC2 for workloads of HPC. Which service is most appropriate?
options: Amazon EBS gp2 with a single instance
AWS Storage Gateway in Tape mode
Amazon FSx for Lustre
Amazon S3 Deep Archive Glacier
questions.explanation: The Amazon FSx for Lustre is optimized for high performance computing workloads (HPC) which require very high throughput and low latency, and can be integrated into S3 as a data layer.

questions.text: A global application needs to route users to the lowest latency endpoint between multiple regions, with automatic failover if a region is unavailable. Route 53 is more suitable?
options: Latency-based Routing combined with health checks
Fixed geographic route, no health checks
Simple Routing (Simple Routing))
Weighted Rotation (Weighted) with Fixed Weight 100% for a single region
questions.explanation: Latency routing directs the user to the Region with less latency; combined with health checks, allows automatic failure to another healthy Region.

questions.text: A table of the DynamoDB face 'hot partitions' because many items share the same key partition, causing throttling even with sufficient capacity. What design strategy best solves this problem?
options: Disable the DynamoDB Streams
To increase the capacity provided indefinitely (RCU/WCU)
Redesign the partition key to better distribute the items (write sharding), for example by adding a random or calculated suffix
Migrate the entire table to the Amazon S3
questions.explanation: Hot partitions occur when the key distribution is uneven. The design solution is to distribute the load by adding a suffix (sharding) to the key partition, spreading the items for more physical partitions.

questions.text: A company performs batch processing workloads that can be paused and resumed, distributed in thousands of instances EC2 of various types, with the aim of minimizing cost. Which approach combines economy and resilience to interruptions?
options: Use only single-type On-Demand instances
Use EC2 Auto Scaling with a combination of Spot Instances of multiple types and instances on-demand as failback (assignment strategy 'capacity-optimized')
Use only Reserved Instances of 3 years
Migrate workload to AWS Lambda No adjustments
questions.explanation: Combine Spot Instances of multiple types/AZs with the "capacity-optimized" strategy and an On-Demand failback significantly reduces costs for interrupt-tolerant loads, maintaining resilience.

questions.text: A company with multiple accounts AWS or optimize costs by taking advantage of discounts per aggregate volume of Savings Plans between all accounts. AWS Organizations allows the sharing of discounts between member accounts?
options: Consolidated Billing)
AWS Configure Aggregator
AWS Resource Access Manager only
Cross-account IAM Roles only
questions.explanation: The Consolidated Billing of AWS Organizations allows you to discounts by volume and benefits of Savings Plans/Reserved Instances are shared between the member accounts, optimizing aggregate costs.

questions.text: A SaaS company B2B you need to allow your corporate client systems (each with its own account) AWS) temporarily access one API internal reading data from a pocket Amazon S3, without sharing long-term credentials and without creating a user IAM per client. Each client must provide a unique identifier to avoid the problem of 'confused deputy'. Which architecture meets these requirements with the lowest risk of security?
options: Create a user IAM dedicated to each client in the SaaS account, generating long-term Access Keys and sharing them via encrypted email.
Create a IAM Role in the SaaS account with a trust policy that allows sts:AssumeRole by customers' accounts, requiring a unique ExternalId value per customer in the condition of the policy.
Returning the Bucket S3 public with a policy that allows reading of any main authenticated in AWS (Main: "*" with condition aws:MainType=AWS).
Configure AWS Organizations to place each client's account as a member of the SaaS organization and use one SCP to free up access to the pocket.
questions.explanation: The use of AssumeRole between accounts with the sts:ExternalId condition is the standard recommended by AWS for integrations of third parties, because it generates temporary credentials via STS and the unique ExternalId per client prevents a malicious client from prompting SaaS to take over the role on behalf of another client (confused deputy)).
questions.hint: Think of the pattern of account access that uses temporary credentials via STS and a condition that uniquely identifies who is requesting access.
optionRationales: The use of AssumeRole between accounts with the sts:ExternalId condition is the standard recommended by AWS for integrations of third parties, because it generates temporary credentials via STS and the unique ExternalId per client prevents a malicious client from prompting SaaS to take over the role on behalf of another client (confused deputy)).

Long-term Access Keys violate the principle of lower exposure of credentials, require constant manual rotation and do not scale operationally to multiple clients, besides not solving the problem of confused deputy.

Make the bucket accessible to any authenticated principal in AWS exposes data to all accounts AWS of the world, a serious security failure that does not meet the requirement of restricted access per customer.

It is neither feasible nor desirable to add external client accounts to the organization AWS of SaaS, because this implies in centralized management of billing and governance that the client would not accept, in addition to SCPs do not grant permission, only restrict what is already allowed.

questions.text: A financial institution stores extremely sensitive encrypted data with the Amazon S3 using SSE-KMS. Compliance policy requires the company to have complete control over the life cycle of encryption keys, including the ability to immediately disable a key to make all associated objects inaccessible (kill switch), and to audit in detail each encryption/description operation.?
options: Use Customer Managed Keys on AWS KMS, with restrictive key policies, allowing to disable or schedule the key deletion and auditing the use via AWS CloudTrail.
Use AWS managed keys (aws/s3) of the KMS, because they already provide tracking of use in CloudTrail and may be excluded by the customer when necessary.
Use SSE-S3 (keys managed by AWS) to simplify the operation, since the encryption AES-256 is equivalent in safety and auditability to SSE-KMS.
Implement client-side encryption with a custom library before uploading to S3, storing keys in a database RDS separate.
questions.explanation: Customer Managed Keys no KMS give the customer total control over key policy, rotation, enable/disable and delete key; all calls kms:Decrypt and kms:GenerateDataKey are individually registered in CloudTrail, allowing granular audit and an immediate kill switch when disabled key.
questions.hint: The granular control over enabling/disableing and auditing an encryption key is directly linked to who is the administrative key owner in the key management service.
optionRationales: Customer Managed Keys no KMS give the customer total control over key policy, rotation, enable/disable and delete key; all calls kms:Decrypt and kms:GenerateDataKey are individually registered in CloudTrail, allowing granular audit and an immediate kill switch when disabled key.

♪ Out of the way SSE-S3 also use AES-256, the keys are fully managed by the AWS without customer-configurable key policies, without customer-driven granular disabling capacity and without individual key-use registration in the CloudTrail, not meeting the control and audit requirements.

AWS managed keys cannot be disabled, have their policy edited or be excluded by the customer; the life cycle is entirely controlled by AWS, what does not meet the requirement of immediate kill switch under customer control.

Building a custom key management system introduces significantly higher operational and security risks than using the KMS, which is already validated for FIPS 140-2 and offers managed HSMs, without the need to reinvent this infrastructure.

questions.text: An application executed in instances Amazon EC2 within private sub-networks (no route to a Internet Gateway or NAT Gateway) needs to read and record objects in a pocket Amazon S3 The security team requires that this traffic never cross the public internet and that access to the ticket is restricted only to requests originating from that VPC, even if they are credentials IAM valid are compromised and used from another location. What combination of configurations meets TODOS requirements?
options: Attach managed AmazonS3FullAccess to the Role policy IAM of the bodies EC2 and rely only on the principle of least privilege of permissions IAM.
Use AWS Direct Connect to create a dedicated connection between the VPC and service Amazon S3.
Create a Gateway VPC Endpoint for the Amazon S3 and add to the policy of the bucket a condition that denies access to unless aws:SourceVpce matches the endpoint ID.
Provide one NAT Gateway in the public sub-network and update the route table of the private sub-network to point 0.0.0.0/0 for the NAT Gateway.
questions.explanation: The Gateway VPC Endpoint S3 allows private traffic between VPC and the S3 no use NAT Gateway or Internet Gateway, and the condition aws:SourceVpce in the pocket policy ensures that even with valid credentials, access is only allowed if originated by this specific endpoint, blocking external attempts.
questions.hint: Consider a network mechanism that maintains traffic for a service AWS inside the backbone of the AWS and a resource policy condition based on the origin of such traffic.
optionRationales: The Gateway VPC Endpoint S3 allows private traffic between VPC and the S3 no use NAT Gateway or Internet Gateway, and the condition aws:SourceVpce in the pocket policy ensures that even with valid credentials, access is only allowed if originated by this specific endpoint, blocking external attempts.

Although the NAT Gateway allow private sub-networks to access the S3 by public internet (via its public endpoint), this violates the requirement that traffic never cross the public internet and does not restrict access to the ticket by network origin.

Permissions IAM control 'who' can access, but do not prevent the same credentials from being used from outside the VPC if they are committed; the explicit requirement to restrict by network origin requires a condition based on VPC Endpoint in Resource Policy.

The AWS Direct Connect is designed to connect on-premises data centers to AWS via dedicated circuit, not being the appropriate mechanism for private traffic between resources within itself VPC and services AWS regional S3, which is solved via VPC Endpoints.

questions.text: A development team stores a database password Amazon RDS for PostgreSQL no AWS Secrets Manager. Security policy requires automatic rotation of credentials for each 30 days without downtime of the application and without manual intervention, in addition to versioning the credentials to allow rollback in case of rotation failure. Which solution fully meets this requirement with the least implementation effort?
options: Configure native autorotation AWS Secrets Manager for RDS, using the function Lambda of managed rotation provided by AWS, with a schedule of 30 days.
Store password in AWS Systems Manager Parameter Store as a SecureString parameter and create a cron job in an instance EC2 to manually alter it every month.
Disable password authentication RDS and use only Security Groups to control access to the database.
Encode the bank password directly into the application source code and update the Git repository to each 30 days via IC/CD pipeline.
questions.explanation: The AWS Secrets Manager has function templates Lambda Rotation ready specifically for the Amazon RDS, implementing the multi-step rotation strategy (createsecret, setsecret, testsecret, finishsecret) with automatic versioning (AWSCURRENT/AWSPENDING/AWSPREVIOUS), allowing downtime and rollback rotation through secret versions.
questions.hint: Look for the service that already comes with integration and pre-built rotation functions specifically for managed databases of the AWS.
optionRationales: The AWS Secrets Manager has function templates Lambda Rotation ready specifically for the Amazon RDS, implementing the multi-step rotation strategy (createsecret, setsecret, testsecret, finishsecret) with automatic versioning (AWSCURRENT/AWSPENDING/AWSPREVIOUS), allowing downtime and rollback rotation through secret versions.

The Parameter Store has no native automatic rotation integrated into the life cycle of the RDS; a solution based on cron job manual in EC2 introduces a single point of failure, high operational effort and risk of inconsistency between the stored secret and the bank's real password.

Disable password authentication without setting alternative authentication (such as IAM Database Authentication) would leave the bank inaccessible or unsafe; Security Groups control network access, do not replace the need for authentication credentials in the bank.

Store credentials directly in the source code is a classic unsafe practice that exposes secrets in the versioning history and in any environment where the code is implemented, besides not providing automatic rotation or secure versioning.

questions.text: A public web application exposed through a Application Load Balancer (ALB) has suffered volumetric layer attacks 7 (HTTP (flood) originating from a large number of different IP addresses, in addition to recurrent attempts to SQL injection. The company is also a customer of a plan that offers specialized support from the DDoS Response team (DRT) of AWS during incidents. What combination of services mitigates AMBOS the types of attack and provides access to specialized support?
options: Linking ALB to one AWS WAF Web ACL with rules managed for SQL injection and a rate-based rule (rate-based rule), in addition to signing AWS Shield Advanced.
Migrate application to instances EC2 with Elastic IP and configure Security Groups to allow only traffic from a fixed list of reliable IPs.
Enable only the AWS Shield Standard, which is already activated automatically and offers complete protection against layer attacks 7 and SQL injection without additional cost.
Configure Network ACLs in the sub-network of the ALB to block all traffic HTTP door entry 80 and 443.
questions.explanation: The AWS WAF with managed rules (Managed Rule Groups) blocks known patterns of SQL injection while a rate-based rule mitigates HTTP floods limiting IP requests of origin; AWS Shield Advanced adds advanced layered DDoS protection 3/4/7 and gives access to the DDoS Response Team (DRT) during incidents.
questions.hint: Think of an application filtering layer that understands requisition patterns HTTP combined with a DDoS protection service that includes specialized human support.
optionRationales: The AWS WAF with managed rules (Managed Rule Groups) blocks known patterns of SQL injection while a rate-based rule mitigates HTTP floods limiting IP requests of origin; AWS Shield Advanced adds advanced layered DDoS protection 3/4/7 and gives access to the DDoS Response Team (DRT) during incidents.

The AWS Shield Standard automatically protects against the most common DDoS network and transport attacks (layers) 3 and 4), but does not include protection against application layer attacks as SQL injection does not offer access to the DDoS Response Team, which is an exclusive benefit of Shield Advanced.
Lock the doors 80 and 443 would make the web application completely inaccessible to legitimate users, being an unviable solution that does not distinguish malicious traffic from legitimate traffic.

Restricting access to a fixed list of IPs is not feasible for a public web application with diverse users and does not mitigate attacks from SQL injection does not offer specialized support against DDoS, in addition to eliminating the benefits of scalability and traffic distribution from ALB.

questions.text: A great organization has 50 accounts AWS organized in multiple organizational units (OUs) in AWS Organizations, representing different departments. The IT team wants all the 2.000 employees log in once using the corporate identity provider (Microsoft Enter ID via SAML) and, from a single portal, they can assume different levels of access (only reading, administrator, financial) in specific accounts, without creating users. IAM which solution meets this requirement with a lower administrative burden?
options: Configure the AWS IAM Identity Center (successor to AWS SSO) integrated with Microsoft Sign in ID via SAML 2.0, defining Permission Reusable Sets and assigning them to user groups for specific accounts within the organization.
Use Service Control Policies (SCPs) no AWS Organizations to grant read, admin and financial access permissions directly to employees.
Manually Create a User IAM in each of the 50 accounts for each of the 2.000 employees, totaling 100.000 users IAM, with individual policies.
Enable Amazon Cognito User Pools in the organization's management account and use groups from Cognito to map permissions IAM in each member account.
questions.explanation: The IAM Identity Center centralizes federated authentication via SAML with the Entra ID and allows to define Permission Sets (sets of reusable permissions, such as ReadOnly, AdministratorAccess or Customized) assigned to user groups per account, eliminating the need for users IAM individual and providing a single access portal (AWS portal access).
questions.hint: The right service centralizes the federation SAML corporate and uses reusable 'permission sets' for multiple accounts within an organization.
optionRationales: The IAM Identity Center centralizes federated authentication via SAML with the Entra ID and allows to define Permission Sets (sets of reusable permissions, such as ReadOnly, AdministratorAccess or Customized) assigned to user groups per account, eliminating the need for users IAM individual and providing a single access portal (AWS portal access).
This approach is operationally impossible on a scale, requiring manual management of 100.000 identities, no single sign-on real and violating good practices of centralized identity management.

SCPs define the maximum permissions that member accounts may have, but do not grant permissions to identities or provide authentication or federation of users; they do not replace a user access management system.

The Amazon Cognito is aimed at authentication of end users of applications (mobile/web), not for corporate identity federation of employees accessing the console and multiple accounts AWS way SSO; o IAM Identity Center is the service designed for this use case.

questions.text: A startup is developing a mobile app that allows users to log in with their Google or Facebook accounts and, after authenticated, upload photos directly to a pocket Amazon S3 and record records in a table of Amazon DynamoDB, each user accessing only their own data. The team does not want to manage any backend of their own authentication or expose long-term credentials in the application. Which architecture meets these requirements?
options: Use Amazon Cognito User Pools for federated authentication with Google and Facebook as identity providers, and Cognito Identity Pools to exchange identity tokens for temporary credentials of AWS STS with restricted permissions via IAM roles and policies with context variables of Cognito.
Use AWS IAM Identity Center to federate end users of the mobile app via Google and Facebook, assigning permission sets access to the S3 and DynamoDB.
Create a IAM Role with AmazonS3FullAccess and AmazonDynamoDBFullAccess policy, and embed the Access Keys of this role directly into the mobile app source code.
Implement a custom authentication server in an instance EC2 that validates tokens on Google/Facebook and directly generates Access Keys IAM permanent for each user.
questions.explanation: Cognito User Pools manages the federation with external identity providers (Google, Facebook) without its own backend, while Identity Pools provides temporary credentials from STS; political IAM with the variable cognito-identity.amazonaws.com:sub allow you to restrict each user's access to your own objects S3 (by prefix) and DynamoDB (by partition key), with no long-term credentials.
questions.hint: Think of the service focused on end-user identities of applications that combines social identity providers with the issuance of temporary credentials from AWS.
optionRationales: Cognito User Pools manages the federation with external identity providers (Google, Facebook) without its own backend, while Identity Pools provides temporary credentials from STS; political IAM with the variable cognito-identity.amazonaws.com:sub allow you to restrict each user's access to your own objects S3 (by prefix) and DynamoDB (by partition key), with no long-term credentials.

Embed long-term Access Keys into a mobile application is an extremely unsafe practice, as the code can be decompiled, exposing credentials with full access to S3 and DynamoDB for any user of the app, without isolation between users.

Building and maintaining a custom authentication server adds unnecessary operational complexity and security risk when the Cognito already offers this functionality in a managed way, besides generating Permanent Access Keys being an unrecommended practice.

The IAM Identity Center is designed to provide access to the console's workforce (staff) and accounts AWS way SSO corporate, not for authentication of end users of consumer applications; Amazon Cognito is the appropriate service for this use case.

questions.text: An e-commerce company exposes its website through a Application Load Balancer with a certificate TLS issued for the domain www.lojaexemplo.com.br. The security team requires that the certificate be automatically renewed before it expires without manual intervention and that communication between users and the ALB be always encrypted (HTTPS), with automatic rerouting of requests HTTP for HTTPS. What solution requires the least continuous operational effort for certificate management?
options: Buy a certificate from an external certifying authority, upload manual to IAM as a server certificate (IAM Server Certificate Store) and associate it with ALB.
Configure the Amazon Route 53 with a record of aliases pointing to ALB and depend on DNSSEC to provide cryptography in transit without using certificates TLS no ALB.
Generate a self-signed certificate using OpenSSL in an instance EC2 and configure it not ALB to avoid costs with certifying authorities.
Request a public certificate at AWS Certificate Manager (ACM) with validation DNS, associate it with a listener HTTPS (443) no ALB, and set up a listener HTTP (80) with a redirection rule for HTTPS.
questions.explanation: Certificates issued by ACM with validation DNS are automatically renewed by AWS before expiry, without any manual intervention, provided that the registration CNAME validation remains in the Route 53 (or DNS equivalent); or ALB supports listener rules to redirect HTTP for HTTPS native.
questions.hint: Look for the managed certificate service from AWS which is natively integrated into load balancers and automatically renews certificates when issued with validation by DNS.
optionRationales: Certificates issued by ACM with validation DNS are automatically renewed by AWS before expiry, without any manual intervention, provided that the registration CNAME validation remains in the Route 53 (or DNS equivalent); or ALB supports listener rules to redirect HTTP for HTTPS native.

Certificates manually loaded no IAM (Server Certificate Store) are not automatically renewed; the team would need to repeat the manual process of purchase, upload and association before each expiration, increasing the operational effort and the undetected risk of expiration.

Self-signed certificates are unreliable by browsers and require users to ignore safety warnings, as well as need manual renewal, which does not meet production requirements for a public e-commerce site.

DNSSEC protects the integrity of the answers DNS against falsification, but does not provide transport layer encryption (TLS) for traffic HTTP between the browser and ALB; is a safety mechanism of DNS, not a substitute for certificates TLS.

questions.text: The security team of an organization with 40 accounts no AWS Organizations Wants to ensure that NENHUMA member count, including the root user of these accounts, can disable the AWS CloudTrail, exclude existing audit trails or exit the organization, even if administrative credentials are compromised. What approach does this control apply in a preventive and comprehensive way in all accounts?
options: Enable log file integrity validation (log file validation) in CloudTrail to detect adulterations in log files stored in S3.

Create a Service Control Policy (SCP) attached to the root of the organization (or to an OR containing all accounts) which explicitly denies the actions cloudtrail:StopLogging, cloudtrail:DeleteTrail and organizations:LeaveOrganization for all main players.
Configure a rule of AWS Configure to monitor the status of CloudTrail and manage a notification via Amazon SNS when logging is disabled.
Attaching a Policy IAM managed to all administrative roles of each account denying the shares cloudtrail:StopLogging, cloudtrail:DeleteTrail and organizations:LeaveOrganization.
questions.explanation: SCPs define the maximum permission limit for all identities of a member account, including root user, and cannot be replaced by policies IAM local; one SCP of explicit denial (deny) in these actions blocks preventively any attempt, even by administrators with compromised credentials.
questions.hint: Think of the only type of policy that can restrict permissions even to the root user of a member account, centrally throughout the organization.
optionRationales: SCPs define the maximum permission limit for all identities of a member account, including root user, and cannot be replaced by policies IAM local; one SCP of explicit denial (deny) in these actions blocks preventively any attempt, even by administrators with compromised credentials.

Policies IAM do not apply to the root user of the account and may be modified or removed by an administrator with sufficient permissions (including an attacker with compromised credentials), not offering a comprehensive preventive guarantee as a SCP.

The AWS Config with this rule only detects and notifys after the fact (reactive/detective approach), not preventing the action to disable the CloudTrail is, which does not meet the prevention requirement.

Log integrity validation only ensures that stored log files have not been changed after recording, but does not prevent someone from stopping logging or deleting the log path from CloudTrail before new events are recorded.

questions.text: A company needs to continuously ensure that all the newsletters S3 set up in any of the following: 25 your organization's accounts follow a set of compliance rules based on CIS AWS Foundations Benchmark (e.g. public access lock, enabled encryption). In addition to detecting non-compliant buckets, the solution must automatically correct buckets that are created with public access enabled, without manual intervention. What solution meets this requirement in a scalable way throughout the organization?
options: Enable AWS Trusted Advisor with the Business plan in each account and manually review the security checks related to buckets S3 public every week.

Implement a Compliance Pack of AWS Config (based on the template of CIS AWS Foundations Benchmark) via AWS Organizations, combining managed config rules with automatic config remediation actions AWS Systems Manager Automation to fix non-compliant pocketes.
Enable AWS CloudTrail on all accounts and use Amazon Athena to consult the logs in search of operations to create buckets S3 public.
Request each development team to manually document the configuration of their newsletters S3 in a shared spreadsheet, reviewed quarterly by the security team.
questions.explanation: Conformity Packages AWS Config can be implemented throughout the organization from the management account, grouping compliance rules (such as checking public access in buckets S3) with automatic remediation via SSM Automation, correcting configuration deviations without manual and scale intervention.
questions.hint: Look for a service that continuously evaluates resource configuration against a set of predefined rules and can be combined with correction automations, centrally deployable throughout the organization.
optionRationales: Conformity Packages AWS Config can be implemented throughout the organization from the management account, grouping compliance rules (such as checking public access in buckets S3) with automatic remediation via SSM Automation, correcting configuration deviations without manual and scale intervention.

The Trusted Advisor provides useful checks on buckets S3 with public access, but does not offer automatic remediation or native aggregation on an organizational scale with continuous application of policies; depends on periodic manual review, not being an automated and continuous solution.

The CloudTrail with Athena allows forensic and investigative analyses after the fact, but does not continuously evaluate the configuration of resources against a compliance framework nor performs automatic remedying.

A manual process based on non-scale spreadsheets for 25 accounts, does not detect real-time deviations and does not offer any automatic remedial action, going against the requirement of automatic correction of non-compliant buckets.

questions.text: A company with 35 accounts AWS organized not AWS Organizations it wants its central security team, located in a dedicated security account, to have unified visibility of threats (such as EC2 communicating with known command and control servers, or possible cryptocurrencies mining) in TODAS the accounts, without having to enable and configure an individual detection service in each account separately. Which approach meets this requirement with the least operational effort?
options: Enable AWS CloudTrail Lake on the security account and create queries SQL scheduled to identify suspicious patterns of API in all accounts.
Designate the security account as the managing director of the Amazon Macie way AWS Organizations to detect network threats in all accounts.
Enable Amazon GuardDuty individually in each of the 35 accounts and configure each to send notification emails to the security team via Amazon SNS.

Designate the security account as the managing director of the Amazon GuardDuty through the AWS Organizations, automatically enabling or GuardDuty in all existing and future member accounts, with centrally aggregated finding in the security account.
questions.explanation: The Amazon GuardDuty supports native integration with the AWS Organizations, allowing a security account to be designated as a delegated administrator and automatically enable the GuardDuty in all member accounts (current and future), adding all threat finding (such as communication with known malicious IPs or cryptocurrency mining) in a single location.
questions.hint: Think of the threat detection service that has a native managing director model of the AWS Organizations for automatic mass-enabled.
optionRationales: The Amazon GuardDuty supports native integration with the AWS Organizations, allowing a security account to be designated as a delegated administrator and automatically enable the GuardDuty in all member accounts (current and future), adding all threat finding (such as communication with known malicious IPs or cryptocurrency mining) in a single location.

Enable and configure the GuardDuty individually in 35 accounts is operationally costly, prone to account configuration inconsistencies and does not offer an aggregate and centralized view of the finding, requiring the security team to monitor multiple inboxes.

The Amazon Macie is focused on the discovery and classification of sensitive data stored in Amazon S3 (as PII), not in detection of network threats such as communication with command and control infrastructure or cryptocurrency mining, which is the domain of GuardDuty.

The CloudTrail Lake allows you to consult events of API historial, but does not perform behavioral and intelligence analysis of threats in real time (as a correlation with malicious IP feeds) that the GuardDuty provides natively.

questions.text: The security team of an organization with 35 accounts AWS needs a single pane of glass that automatically adds security finders generated by Amazon GuardDuty, AWS Configure and Amazon Inspector in all accounts, and that continuously evaluates the security posture of these accounts against the standard CIS AWS Foundations Benchmark, assigning a compliance score. Which service was specifically designed for this purpose?
options: AWS Security Hub, configured with delegated administrator via AWS Organizations and aggregation between regions, with the safety standard CIS AWS Foundations Benchmark enabled.
Amazon Detective, configured as managing director via AWS Organizations to calculate the conformity score CIS of all accounts.
AWS Audit Manager, collecting evidence automatically from GuardDuty, Configure and Inspector to generate the conformity score CIS in real time.

Develop Functions AWS Lambda customised that periodically consult the APIs of the GuardDuty, Configure and Inspector in each account, storing the results in a table of Amazon DynamoDB and viewing them on a dashboard of Amazon QuickSight.
questions.explanation: The AWS Security Hub is designed to automatically add multiple service finding (GuardDuty, Configure, Inspector, Macie and others) in a standardized format (AWS Security Finding Format), supports delegated administrator for the entire organization, aggregation between regions and calculates a continuous compliance score against standards such as CIS AWS Benchmark Foundations.
questions.hint: Look for the service whose main purpose is to add multiple security finding services to AWS in a standardized format and score compliance against recognized benchmarks.
optionRationales: The AWS Security Hub is designed to automatically add multiple service finding (GuardDuty, Configure, Inspector, Macie and others) in a standardized format (AWS Security Finding Format), supports delegated administrator for the entire organization, aggregation between regions and calculates a continuous compliance score against standards such as CIS AWS Benchmark Foundations.

The Amazon Detective is an investigation tool that helps to analyze and visualize relationships between security finding to discover the root cause of incidents, but does not aggregate multiple service finding in a single panel nor calculates compliance scores against benchmarks such as CIS.

The AWS Audit Manager continuously collects evidence to support formal audits in relation to regulatory frameworks, but its purpose is to generate evidence reports for auditors, not to function as a real-time operating panel that aggregates multiple service security finding.

Build this customized reimplement solution, with significant development and maintenance effort, a functionality that AWS Security Hub already offers natively, managed and with support to multiple accounts via Organizations.

questions.text: During an investigation, the security team identified that a specific IP address is making repeated attempts of brute force against the door 22 (SSH) of several instances EC2 in a sub-network. The team needs to block IMEDIATAMENTE all traffic originating from that IP to TODAS sub-network instances (current and future), without needing to edit the configuration of each Security Group individually, since there are dozens of Security Groups which mechanism allows this?
options: Create a Web ACL of the AWS WAF associated with fora EC2 with a rule that locks the IP address on the door 22.
Add a denial rule (deny) to the IP address of origin at Network ACL associated with the sub-network, with a lower priority (rule number) than existing permission rules.
Remove Internet Gateway of VPC to cut off all external connectivity until the attack stops.
Add a denial rule (deny) to the original IP address on the door 22 in each of the Security Groups associated with sub-network instances.
questions.explanation: Network ACLs operate at the level of the sub-network, are statesss and support explicit rules of DENY, being evaluated before the Security Groups; a deny rule with low priority number (evaluated first) immediately blocks the traffic of this IP for all sub-network instances, current and future, without need to change multiples Security Groups.
questions.hint: Think about the network security component that operates at the sub-network level, is evaluated before the Security Groups and is the only one who supports explicit rules of denial.
optionRationales: Network ACLs operate at the level of the sub-network, are statesss and support explicit rules of DENY, being evaluated before the Security Groups; a deny rule with low priority number (evaluated first) immediately blocks the traffic of this IP for all sub-network instances, current and future, without need to change multiples Security Groups.

Security Groups support only permission rules (allow); it is not possible to create a deny rule in a Security Group, making this approach technically impossible, in addition to requiring the editing of dozens of Security Groups individually.

Remove Internet Gateway would interrupt all connectivity from entering and leaving the internet to the VPC whole, affecting legitimate users and services, a disproportionate action compared to blocking a single malicious IP.

The AWS WAF operates in the application layer (HTTP/HTTPS) and can only be associated with Amazon CloudFront, Application Load Balancer, API Gateway or AWS AppSync, unable to filter traffic SSH (door 22) directly to for instance EC2.

questions.text: A company is migrating to a microservices architecture in containers, where hundreds of services need to authenticate each other using mTLS (TLS The company does not want to operate its own infrastructure for the construction of a new plant. PKI (root key generation, secure storage, recall lists), but you need to keep complete control over the hierarchy of certificates, which should never be publicly exposed. What service meets this requirement?
options: AWS Certificate Manager Private Certificate Authority (ACM Private CA), by creating a private CA hierarchy to issue short-term certificates for microservices, with integration into ACM for life cycle management.
Configure your own CA root using OpenSSL in an instance EC2 dedicated, storing CA's private key in a volume EBS encrypted and hand-distributed certificates for each microservice.
AWS Certificate Manager (ACM) public, requesting public certificates validated by DNS for each of the internal microservices.
Store a single wildcard certificate in AWS Secrets Manager and share it among all microservices for mTLS authentication.
questions.explanation: The ACM Private CA provides an infrastructure of PKI fully managed for the issuance of private certificates (not publicly reliable), allowing to create root/subordinate CA hierarchies, issue short-term certificates for mTLS between microservices, and integrates to ACM for distribution and renewal, without the company having to operate its own CA infrastructure.
questions.hint: Search for managed service from AWS offering a complete private certification authority, without requiring the company to operate its own root key infrastructure.
optionRationales: The ACM Private CA provides an infrastructure of PKI fully managed for the issuance of private certificates (not publicly reliable), allowing to create root/subordinate CA hierarchies, issue short-term certificates for mTLS between microservices, and integrates to ACM for distribution and renewal, without the company having to operate its own CA infrastructure.

Public certificates of the ACM require publicly resolvable domain validation and are intended for publicly exposed endpoints; issuing hundreds of public certificates for internal communication between microservices is not appropriate, scalable or in line with the requirement that certificates never be publicly exposed.

This approach requires the company to operate its own infrastructure of PKI, including generation and protection of the root key, issue, distribution and revocation of certificates, going exactly against the requirement not to operate own CA infrastructure.

The AWS Secrets Manager store secrets, but does not issue certificates or manage a CA hierarchy; moreover, sharing a single wildcard certificate among hundreds of services eliminates the individual identity required by mTLS and creates a single point of failure if compromised.

questions.text: An internal platform allows development teams to create their own IAM roles and policies for the microservices that they build (self-service model). The platform team needs to ensure that, regardless of how permissive the policy that a team attaches to a role created by it, this role NUNCA may, for example, access billing data, create new users IAM or access resources from other teams — a maximum limit of permissions that applies to all roles created in this way. IAM meets this requirement?
options: Configure a standardized boundary permissions and require, via policy IAM with condition in iam:CreateRole, that every role created by the teams has this boundary attached; the effective permissions of the roll will be the intersection between its policy and the boundary.
Create Service Control Policies (SCPs) individual for each development team, restricting the actions that each team can include in its own policies IAM.
Create a single IAM role shared with AdministratorAccess policy that all development teams assume to implement their microservices.
Grant Managed Policy AdministratorAccess to all development teams and rely on manual infrastructure code revisions (IaC) before deployment to detect excessive permissions.
questions.explanation: Boundary permissions define the maximum permission limit that a managed identity (role or user) may have; when requiring, by condition in iam:CreateRole, that every role created by teams includes this boundary, ensures that, regardless of the policy annexed by the team, effective permissions never exceed what the boundary allows — exactly the requirement of a ceiling of permissions for creating self-service roles.
questions.hint: Think of the mechanism of IAM defining a ceiling of permissions applied to the intersection with the policy attached to identity, allowing secure delegation of the creation of roles.
optionRationales: Boundary permissions define the maximum permission limit that a managed identity (role or user) may have; when requiring, by condition in iam:CreateRole, that every role created by teams includes this boundary, ensures that, regardless of the policy annexed by the team, effective permissions never exceed what the boundary allows — exactly the requirement of a ceiling of permissions for creating self-service roles.

SCPs are applied at the account level or OR within the AWS Organizations and affect all the main accounts in a homogeneous way; they were not designed to impose, in a differentiated way, a specific permission ceiling for roles created dynamically by different teams within the same account..

Granting AdministratorAccess violates the principle of lesser privilege from the beginning, and relying on manual code revision is a reactive process and subject to human error, not a technical guarantee that the permission limit will never be exceeded.

Sharing a single role with AdministratorAccess among all teams eliminates any isolation of permissions between teams, violates the principle of lesser privilege and offers no configurable maximum limit mechanism per role.

questions.text: A SaaS company B2B offers a data analysis service that runs behind a Network Load Balancer in your own VPC. She needs to allow hundreds of corporate clients, each with their own VPC (many with blocks CIDR This is the first time that the Commission has been able to take a decision on a proposal from the Commission to the Council (COM(93) 564 final — Doc. VPC internal to customers. Which architecture meets this requirement in a scalable way?
options: Exposing the Network Load Balancer publicly with an Elastic IP and restrict access through a list of allowed IPs (allowlists) in Security Groups.
Establish VPC Peering between the VPC of SaaS and the VPC of each of the hundreds of customers.
Connect to VPC of SaaS and the VPCs of all customers to a AWS Transit Gateway shared.
Create a AWS PrivateLink VPC Endpoint Service pointing to Network Load Balancer existing, and each client creates an Interface VPC Endpoint in your own VPC to connect to the service.
questions.explanation: The AWS PrivateLink allows a service provider to display an application through a VPC Endpoint Service based on a NLB; customers consume the service by creating Interface VPC Endpoints in their own VPCs, without needing to peering, without exposing the VPC the entire provider, without crossing the public internet, and even works with ICDRs superimposed between the VPCs of the customers, because there is no direct network routing between them.
questions.hint: Think of the private connectivity mechanism designed specifically for service provider/consumer (SaaS) models, which does not require compatible CIDRs between the networks involved.
optionRationales: The AWS PrivateLink allows a service provider to display an application through a VPC Endpoint Service based on a NLB; customers consume the service by creating Interface VPC Endpoints in their own VPCs, without needing to peering, without exposing the VPC the entire provider, without crossing the public internet, and even works with ICDRs superimposed between the VPCs of the customers, because there is no direct network routing between them.

VPC Peering requires blocks CIDR not overlapping between connected VPCs (which is not guaranteed among customers), exposes wider network routes than just the specific service, and does not scale well to manage hundreds of individual peering connections.

The Transit Gateway centralizes the route between multiple VPCs, but also requires CIDRs not overlapping between connected VPCs and creates network connectivity wider than what is needed to only consume a specific service, in addition to requiring customers to share network connectivity with SaaS infrastructure.

Exposing the NLB publicly causes traffic to cross the public internet, which directly violates the requirement that traffic should never pass through the public internet, in addition to requiring constant maintenance of an IP allow list of hundreds of customers.

questions.text: A company operates dozens of VPCs spread across multiple accounts AWS, all connected to one AWS Transit Gateway in a hub-and-spoke topology. The security team needs to centrally and stately (stateful) inspect all the outbound traffic to the internet originating from these VPCs, including intrusion prevention capabilities (IPS) and filtering of malicious domains, before traffic goes out through a NAT Gateway which architecture meets this requirement?
options: Configure Deny Rules Security Groups of each VPC Spoke to block known malicious domains.

Implant AWS Network Firewall in a VPC Centralized inspection connected to the Transit Gateway, configuring the route tables of the Spoke VPCs to send out traffic through the VPC inspection before reaching the NAT Gateway.
Implant one NAT Gateway individual VPC spoke and analyze the VPC Flow Logs with Amazon Athena to identify suspicious traffic.
Linking a Web ACL of the AWS WAF each VPC Spoke to inspect all outbound traffic.
questions.explanation: The AWS Network Firewall offers stateful traffic inspection with rules of intrusion prevention (compatible with Suricata) and domain filtering; by centralizing it in a VPC of connected inspection via Transit Gateway in hub-and-spoke topology, all output traffic of the spoke VPCs can be routed through it before reaching the NAT Gateway, meeting the requirement of centralized inspection with state.
questions.hint: Think about the state-of-the-art network firewall service with IPS and domain filtering, which can be centralized in a hub-and-spoke topology based on Transit Gateway.
optionRationales: The AWS Network Firewall offers stateful traffic inspection with rules of intrusion prevention (compatible with Suricata) and domain filtering; by centralizing it in a VPC of connected inspection via Transit Gateway in hub-and-spoke topology, all output traffic of the spoke VPCs can be routed through it before reaching the NAT Gateway, meeting the requirement of centralized inspection with state.
Security Groups do not support denial rules (only allow) and do not have domain filtering or intrusion prevention capacity; this approach is technically unfeasible for the requirement presented.
VPC Flow Logs with Athena provide visibility after the fact (forense/analytics), but do not offer real-time inspection with IPS they don't actively block malicious traffic before it goes online..

The AWS WAF operates in the application layer and can only be associated with specific resources such as CloudFront, ALB, API Gateway or AppSync; it cannot be associated with a VPC to inspect general output traffic at network level.

questions.text: A company's security policy completely prohibits the opening of any inbound door Security Groups for administrative access (SSH/RDP), including from bastion hosts, and requires that all commands executed by administrators in instances EC2 are registered and audited. The instances are in private sub-networks, without public IP. TODOS these requirements?
options: Configure a connection AWS Site-to-Site VPN between the corporate network and VPC, and allow SSH directly to the private IPs of the instances through the VPN.

Use AWS Systems Manager Session Manager, with the SSM Agent installed in the instances and a role IAM with the necessary permissions, allowing shell connections via console/CLI without the need for open entrance doors, and enabling the registration of sessions in the Amazon CloudWatch Logs or Amazon S3.
Implant a bastion host in a public sub-network with a Security Group allowing SSH (door 22) only from the corporate IP range.
Use EC2 Connect Forum to establish connections SSH temporary certified via IAM.
questions.explanation: Session Manager establishes connection via output calls (outbound) HTTPS) of the SSM Officer for service Systems Manager (or via VPC Interface Endpoint), completely eliminating the need for open entry doors in Security Groups, Public IPs or bastion hosts, and records all commands and outputs of sessions for full audit.
questions.hint: Think of the managed service that establishes administrative sessions using only instance output connections, eliminating the need for input ports and providing native session logs.
optionRationales: Session Manager establishes connection via output calls (outbound) HTTPS) of the SSM Officer for service Systems Manager (or via VPC Interface Endpoint), completely eliminating the need for open entry doors in Security Groups, Public IPs or bastion hosts, and records all commands and outputs of sessions for full audit.

Even restricted to a corporate IP range, this approach still requires an open entry rule on the door 22, directly violating the policy prohibiting any entry door for administrative access, in addition to adding an additional host to manage and protect.

Although the VPN provide an encrypted tunnel, it would still be necessary to open the door 22 no Security Groups for the CIDR of VPN, violating the policy of no entry door for administrative access, and this approach does not offer native registration of commands executed in sessions.

The EC2 Connect Forum still depends on a connection SSH traditional doorway 22, requiring a rule of entry into Security Group releasing this port to the service IP tracks, and does not provide native session command log equivalent to Session Manager.

questions.text: An application encrypts data on the client's side using a customer-managed key (CMK) of the AWS KMS in the us-east region-1 before replicating encrypted data to the eu-west region-1, as part of a disaster recovery strategy. The requirement is that, during a complete unavailability of the us-east region-1, the application in the eu-west region-1 can immediately describe the data, without making any call from API for the us-east region-1. What configuration of the KMS meets this requirement?
options: During failure, describe all replicated data using the CMK Of us-east-1 before unavailability and re-encrypt them with a new CMK created in eu-west-1.
Use AWS managed key standard (aws/s3) in both regions, since keys managed by the AWS are automatically replicated between regions.
Create a multi-Region key KMS (multi-Region key) with the primary key in us-east-1 and a replica key in me-west-1, sharing the same cryptographic material and related key ID.
Create a CMK of single region in us-east-1 and use grants from KMS to grant description permissions to principals in the account used by the application in eu-west-1.
questions.explanation: Multi-Region Keys KMS allow to create a primary key in one region and replicas in other regions that share the same cryptographic material; data encrypted with the primary key can be described using the local replica key in eu-west-1, without any call from API for us-east-1, even during a total unavailability of the primary region.
questions.hint: Think about the resource of KMS which allows the same key material to exist independently in multiple regions, eliminating the dependence of calls between regions during the description.
optionRationales: Multi-Region Keys KMS allow to create a primary key in one region and replicas in other regions that share the same cryptographic material; data encrypted with the primary key can be described using the local replica key in eu-west-1, without any call from API for us-east-1, even during a total unavailability of the primary region.

Keys KMS of the unique region exist only in the region where they were created; even with grants granting permissions, the operation kms:Decrypt for this key would still need to be executed against the endpoint of KMS in us-east-1, what would be impossible during a total unavailability of this region.

AWS managed keys are specific to each region and service account, and are not replicated between regions; each region has its own AWS managed independent key, which does not share cryptographic material with that of another region.

This approach would require pre-processing and re-encryption of all data in advance (does not meet the scenario of sudden unavailability) and does not resolve the requirement that the description occurs without dependence on the us-east region.-1 at the moment of failure.

questions.text: Account A has a snapshot of Amazon EBS Encrypted with a customer-managed key (CMK) of the AWS KMS belonging to Account A. The team needs to share this snapshot with Account B so that it can create volumes EBS and launch instances EC2 from it. What actions are needed for Account B to be able to use this encrypted snapshot successfully?
options: Make the snapshot public so any account AWS can use it, simplifying the sharing process.

Modify snapshot permissions to share it with Account B, and update the policy CMK from Account A (or add a grant) to allow Account B principals to use the shares kms:CreateGrant, kms:Decrypt and kms:DescribeKey about this key.
Create an unencrypted copy of the snapshot in Account A before sharing it with Account B, eliminating the dependency of KMS.

Just modify the snapshot permissions in Account A to share it with Account B ID, without any change in KMS, since snapshot sharing already automatically includes access to the associated encryption key.
questions.explanation: Sharing only the snapshot permission is not enough when it is encrypted with a CMK Customer: Account B also needs permission to use the CMK from Account A to describe the snapshot data, which requires updating the key policy (or creating a grant) by granting the necessary actions of the KMS to the principals of Account B.
questions.hint: Remember that sharing an encrypted resource between accounts involves two distinct layers of permission: permission over the resource itself and permission over the key that the cryptographer.
optionRationales: Sharing only the snapshot permission is not enough when it is encrypted with a CMK Customer: Account B also needs permission to use the CMK from Account A to describe the snapshot data, which requires updating the key policy (or creating a grant) by granting the necessary actions of the KMS to the principals of Account B.

Sharing an encrypted snapshot does not automatically give access to CMK used to encrypt it; without explicit permissions in the key policy (or a grant) to Account B, attempts to copy or use the snapshot will fail due to lack of permission in KMS.

A AWS does not allow to make public an encrypted snapshot with a CMK of the client — this type of sharing is blocked by design to protect the key material; moreover, making a snapshot public is a bad security practice that exposes the data to any account AWS.

Creating an unencrypted copy of the snapshot would violate compliance requirements that require rest encryption for the data, being a solution that sacrifices security only to avoid the correct configuration of permissions between accounts in KMS.

questions.text: The security team of an organization with 30 accounts AWS needs continuous visibility on which resources — bucks S3, IAM roles, keys to the KMS, functions Lambda and rows SQS — are accessible from outside the organization (external accounts) or publicly, to identify unintentional exposures as soon as possible. The solution should continuously analyze resource-based policies and generate finding automatically. Which service was specifically designed for this purpose?
options: Manually review the policies based on each account's resource every quarter, documenting the findings in an audit report.

AWS IAM Access Analyzer, with an organization-level-configured analytics that continuously evaluates resource-based policies and generates finding whenever a resource is shared with an entity outside the organization or set of trusted accounts.
Create custom rules in AWS Configure for each resource type (S3, IAM, KMS, Lambda, SQS) check manually if the resource policies contain the organization's ID.
AWS Trusted Advisor, enabled in each of 30 accounts, reviewing security checks related to Bucket permissions S3.
questions.explanation: The IAM Access Analyzer uses automated logic reasoning (probable security) to analyze policies based on resource S3, IAM roles, keys to the KMS, functions Lambda, rows SQS and other types of resource, generating continuous finding whenever it detects access granted to entities outside the 'trust zone' (the organisation or account), exactly what the requirement describes.
questions.hint: Think of the service of IAM using automated logical policy analysis to continuously identify shared resources with entities outside a defined confidence zone.
optionRationales: The IAM Access Analyzer uses automated logic reasoning (probable security) to analyze policies based on resource S3, IAM roles, keys to the KMS, functions Lambda, rows SQS and other types of resource, generating continuous finding whenever it detects access granted to entities outside the 'trust zone' (the organisation or account), exactly what the requirement describes.

The Trusted Advisor offers some verifications related to buckets S3 with public access, but does not cover in a comprehensive and continuous way IAM roles, keys to the KMS, functions Lambda and rows SQS regarding external access, it does not offer the same logical analysis of policies on an organizational scale.

Although technically possible, developing and maintaining custom config rules to replicate this policy analysis for each type of resource would require significant development effort, reimplementing a capacity that IAM Access Analyzer already offers native and managed.

A quarterly manual review process does not provide continuous visibility and does not scale to 30 accounts with multiple types of resource, leaving a significant window between the creation of an unintentional exposure and its detection.

questions.text: A financial institution, under strict regulatory requirements, requires that cryptographic material used to protect customer data be stored in hardware security modules (HSM) validated in FIPS 140-2 Level 3, of exclusive use (single-tenant) of the company, with total administrative control over the HSM — in such a way that not even the AWS have access to the key material or the administrative operations of the device. Which service meets this specific requirement?
options: Amazon S3 with encryption on the server side using keys provided by the client (SSE-C), eliminating the need for a HSM managed by AWS.
AWS CloudHSM, providing a cluster of dedicated HSMs (single-tenant) within the VPC company, with the company maintaining exclusive administrative control over the cluster.
AWS KMS with customer-managed keys (Customer Managed Keys), which also use validated HSMs in FIPS 140-2 Level 3 Internally.
AWS Secrets Manager, configured with additional encryption using a CMK Dedicated KMS.
questions.explanation: The AWS CloudHSM provides fora HSM dedicated and single-tenant validated in FIPS 140-2 Level 3, provided within the VPC the customer; the company has total administrative control over the cluster (including management of users of the HSM), and the AWS has no access to the key material or the administrative credentials of the device, precisely meeting the requirement of exclusivity and total control.
questions.hint: The essential difference is between a fully managed cryptography service and multi-tenant versus dedicated hardware of exclusive use, under full customer administrative control.
optionRationales: The AWS CloudHSM provides fora HSM dedicated and single-tenant validated in FIPS 140-2 Level 3, provided within the VPC the customer; the company has total administrative control over the cluster (including management of users of the HSM), and the AWS has no access to the key material or the administrative credentials of the device, precisely meeting the requirement of exclusivity and total control.

Although the AWS KMS uses validated HSMs in FIPS 140-2 Level 3 internally, this is a multi-tenant managed service operated by the AWS, where the AWS controls the infrastructure of the HSM underlying; the customer does not obtain exclusive administrative control of the hardware device, which does not meet the requirement of total exclusivity.

The AWS Secrets Manager is a secret storage and rotation service that internally uses the KMS for encryption; it does not provide, by itself, a dedicated hardware security module and exclusive customer use.

SSE-C requires the customer to manage and provide the encryption keys in each request, transferring all responsibility for safe storage of keys out of the AWS, without providing any infrastructure of HSM validated, which does not meet the requirement of a HSM FIPS 140-2 Level 3 dedicated.

questions.text: A company wants to ensure that, regardless of how an administrator initially authenticated, any attempt to delete the bills S3 production or closure of proceedings EC2 tagged Environment=production requires that the current session has been authenticated with multifactor authentication (MFA) — otherwise, the action should be explicitly denied. What approach implements this control?
options: Attaching a policy to administrative roles IAM with a Deny instruction for the actions s3:Delete Bucket and ec2:TerminateInstructions (with tag condition), using BoolIfExists condition of type "aws:MultiFactorAuthPresent": "false".
Configure the password policy IAM (IAM password policy) to require all users IAM enable MFA before logging into the console.
Enable AWS IAM Identity Center with a requirement for MFA for federated login in the access portal of the AWS.
Enable Amazon S3 Versioning and the protection against closure (Termination Protection) in all instances EC2 Production.
questions.explanation: The global condition aws:MultiFactorAuthPresent allows you to check, at the time of call from API, if the current session has been authenticated with MFA; a Deny instruction with BoolIfExists and this condition defined as false blocks the action specifically when the session does not have MFA, regardless of how the session was originally established, taking into account the verification requirement at the time of the action.
questions.hint: Search for the policy condition of the IAM which checks, at the exact moment of the call from API, if the current session has been authenticated with a second factor.
optionRationales: The global condition aws:MultiFactorAuthPresent allows you to check, at the time of call from API, if the current session has been authenticated with MFA; a Deny instruction with BoolIfExists and this condition defined as false blocks the action specifically when the session does not have MFA, regardless of how the session was originally established, taking into account the verification requirement at the time of the action.

Require MFA in the console login ensures that the initial session is authenticated with MFA, but does not require a specific verification at the time of each call from API sensitive, nor does it apply to programmatic access via long-term access keys, which do not pass through the console login stream.

Require MFA in the federated login of the IAM Identity Center protects the initial establishment of the session, but does not prevent that session (or other sessions without MFA) perform specific destructive actions such as deleting production bucks or closing instances EC2, because there is no political condition linking the action to the presence of MFA in the sitting.

Version S3 and closure protection help to mitigate operational errors and allow recovery after accidental exclusions, but do not impose any requirement of MFA at the time of the action do not explicitly deny the operation for sessions without MFA.

questions.text: A company hosts a static website in a pocket Amazon S3 fully private (with Block Public Access enabled) and distributes it through the Amazon CloudFront. The safety requirement is that the bucket NUNCA can be accessed directly through your URL of the S3 — even if someone discovers the name of the pocket — and that access is only possible through distribution CloudFront company specific. Which configuration meets this requirement without compromising the Block Public Access of the pocket?
options: Configure Origin Access Control (OAC) in the distribution CloudFront for the S3 origin, and update the bucket policy to allow s3:GetObject only when the request comes from this specific distribution, using a condition with aws:SourceArn by reference to ARN of distribution.
Making the public newsletter with a policy that allows s3:GetObject for any major, trusting that users will only know the URL of the CloudFront.
Configure signed URLs no CloudFront, but leave the standard permissions of the bucket S3 unaltered (private, without additional policy for CloudFront).
Create a Bucket Policy that restricts access based on header HTTP Reference sent by requests originating from the CloudFront.
questions.explanation: A Origin Access Control (OAC) allows the CloudFront sign the requests to the S3 using SigV4; Bucket policy can then restrict s3:GetObject exclusively to requests signed by the distribution CloudFront specific (via aws:SourceArn), keeping Block Public Access enabled and ensuring that only CloudFront, and not the URL direct S3, get access to the objects.
questions.hint: Look for the modern mechanism that allows the CloudFront sign your requests to the S3, enabling the policy of the bucket to rely exclusively on this specific distribution.
optionRationales: A Origin Access Control (OAC) allows the CloudFront sign the requests to the S3 using SigV4; Bucket policy can then restrict s3:GetObject exclusively to requests signed by the distribution CloudFront specific (via aws:SourceArn), keeping Block Public Access enabled and ensuring that only CloudFront, and not the URL direct S3, get access to the objects.

To make the newsletter public allows anyone who discovers the URL direct S3 (not just the URL of the CloudFront) access the objects directly, violating the explicit requirement that the bucket should never be accessible via your URL direct, besides requiring to disable the Block Public Access.

Without a Bucket Policy that explicitly grants read permission to CloudFront (way OAC or OAI), the private bucket would also deny access to itself CloudFront, resulting in denied access errors for end users and breaking the site.

Restricting access based on the Referer header is a legacy and easily bypassable technique, as this header can be falsified in direct requests to S3, not offering a security guarantee equivalent to the cryptographic signature of requests provided by Origin Access Control.

questions.text: A company needs to establish encrypted connectivity between its data centre on-premises and a VPC the AWS for a new project with a need for moderate band (under 1.25 Gbps). Transit encryption is a mandatory requirement, and the company cannot wait for the typical time of provisioning of a dedicated physical circuit. What solution meets these requirements of term, band and encryption?
options: Configure VPC Peering between the VPC of AWS and one VPC Emulated on-premises using VMware Cloud on AWS.
Establish a connection AWS Site-to-Site VPN between a customer gateway on-premises and a virtual private gateway (or Transit Gateway) the AWS, using IPsec tunnels on the public internet.
Provide a connection AWS Direct Connect and set up a VPN IPsec on a Virtual Private Interface (VPN over Direct Connect).
Provide a connection AWS Direct Connect with MACsec enabled to ensure encryption in the link layer.
questions.explanation: The AWS Site-to-Site VPN can be provided in minutes to hours, without depending on physical circuit installation, provides native IPsec encryption in transit over the public internet, and comfortably meets moderate bandwidth requirements (each tunnel supports up to approximately 1.25 Gbps), becoming the ideal option for fast and encrypted connectivity.
questions.hint: Compare the provisioning time of a dedicated physical connection to that of an encrypted tunnel established on the public internet.
optionRationales: The AWS Site-to-Site VPN can be provided in minutes to hours, without depending on physical circuit installation, provides native IPsec encryption in transit over the public internet, and comfortably meets moderate bandwidth requirements (each tunnel supports up to approximately 1.25 Gbps), becoming the ideal option for fast and encrypted connectivity.

The AWS Direct Connect requires the provision of a physical cross-connect at a partner location, a process that typically takes weeks to months, which does not meet the requirement to establish connectivity in a few days, regardless of the support to encryption via MACsec.

This approach still depends on the physical provisioning of a connection Direct Connect as a prerequisite, maintaining the same problem from week to month, in addition to adding unnecessary complexity to a need for moderate band and short term.

VPC Peering connects VPCs inside the AWS (including VMware Cloud on environments AWS Accommodation in the AWS), but it's not the standard mechanism to connect a traditional on-premises data center to AWS, and does not solve the requirement of direct hybrid connectivity with encryption in transit.

questions.text: A company created a VPC Endpoint interface for the AWS Secrets Manager, allowing for instances EC2 in private sub-networks recover secrets without internet access. IAM of the instances has wide permissions in the Secrets Manager (secretsmanager:GetSecretValue in "*" features, because it is shared with other purposes. The security team wants to add an extra layer of defense in depth so that, specifically through DESSE endpoint, only the secrets of a specific path (e.g. arn):aws:secretsmanager:*:111122223333:secret:prod/app/*) can be recovered, blocking any other call made by this network path. What configuration implements this additional layer?
options: Reducing the scope of policy IAM of the role of the bodies EC2 to allow secretsmanager:GetSecretValue only in RNAs under prod/app/*.
Configure the Security Group associated with network interface (ENI) of the endpoint to allow only traffic at the door 443 originating in the private sub-network.

Attach an Endpoint Policy (VPC Endpoint Policy) to the Endpoint Interface of Secrets Manager allowing secretsmanager:GetSecretValue only for secret RNAs under the prod/app/* path, implicitly denying all other actions and resources for calls made through this endpoint.
Configure Network ACLs in the sub-network to block all traffic destined for IP bands of Secrets Manager, except for addresses associated with secrets under prod/app/*.
questions.explanation: Policy VPC Endpoint act as an additional and independent layer of permission IAM: a call is only allowed if TANTO policy IAM identity QUANTO the endpoint policy allow. Restricting the endpoint policy to RNAs under prod/app/* ensures that even if the role of the IAM have wider permissions, any call via this endpoint for other secrets be denied — a specific in-depth defense to the network path.
