On-Demand responds to QUALQUER traffic level (including unforeseeable peaks) without capacity planning, which is valuable for IMPRESSIBLE workloads, but has cost POR REQUIREMENT higher than the Provided mode. For a well understood, gradual and PREVIOUS workload, this price award is usually unnecessary — Provided + Auto Scaling offers similar automatic adjustment at a lower cost for predictable patterns.

Incorrect. Provide fixed capacity at the level of PICO means paying for WCU/RCU at peak level throughout the low traffic period of the morning also, when actual use is far below the provided — this is significantly less economical than the Auto Scaling, reducing the capacity provided during periods of low traffic.

Incorrect. DAX is a cache layer of LEITURA; does not alter the capacity needs of ESCRITA of the table, and use DAX to compensate for LEITURA sub-provided solves a different problem (latency/reading cost) than adjusting capacity PROVISIONADA the predictable format of daily traffic — something that the Auto Scaling solves directly.

questions.text: A company executes clusters Amazon EMR for night batch processing jobs with a known deadline (must be completed before business hours). CORE of the cluster (which perform HDFS DataNodes and store data that cannot be lost during the job) are dimensioned to the basic capacity, but the volume of processing varies from night to night, and on peak nights this basic capacity is not enough to complete before the deadline. EXTRA in peak nights to accelerate processing, as economical as possible, accepting that this extra capacity can occasionally be interrupted during the job without catastrophic impact (the processing framework deals with the re-execution of tasks that can be).
options: Add Us TASK (which perform only YARN NodeManagers/Computer, no data HDFS) to the cluster using Spot Instances, dynamically climbing (e.g. via EMR Managed Scaling) according to processing demand
Continuously increase the number of nodes CORE (using On-Demand) to support the expected heavier night volume, every night
Add Us CORE additional use Spot Instances to provide extra capacity on peak nights
Use functions AWS Lambda to deal with excess processing capacity on peak nights
questions.explanation: Right. TASK do not store data from HDFS, then, if a knot TASK in Spot is interrupted, only the tasks in progress in it are lost and re-executed elsewhere by YARN/processing framework (e.g. Spark/Hadoop native failure tolerance), without data loss risk. Use Spot for this extra elastic and interrupt-tolerant capacity provides significant savings compared to On-Demand for the 'peak' capacity required on heavy nights.
questions.hint: Differentiate the role of knots CORE (store data HDFS) of the knots TASK (only computing) when deciding where to apply capacity Spot interruptible.
optionRationales: Right. TASK do not store data from HDFS, then, if a knot TASK in Spot is interrupted, only the tasks in progress in it are lost and re-executed elsewhere by YARN/processing framework (e.g. Spark/Hadoop native failure tolerance), without data loss risk. Use Spot for this extra elastic and interrupt-tolerant capacity provides significant savings compared to On-Demand for the 'peak' capacity required on heavy nights.

Incorrect. CORE execute HDFS DataNodes and store part of the cluster data (including replicated blocks); if a node CORE in Spot is interrupted, this may affect the availability/replication factor of the HDFS, potentially causing job failures or data loss risk — no TASK (which do not store data HDFS) are the appropriate choice for capacity Spot tolerant of interruptions, not us CORE.

Incorrect. Providing permanently for the capacity of the heavier night means paying for that capacity every night, even in the lightest — the opposite of economic for a night-to-night workload; the elastic staggering of us TASK adjusts the capacity to the real demand of each night.

Incorrect. AWS Lambda has a limit of execution time (15 minutes) and was not designed to integrate as additional computational capacity within a cluster EMR/Hadoop/YARN existing — restructure surplus processing as functions Lambda separate would require a fundamentally different processing model from the batch job based on EMR existing.

questions.text: A company is migrating to the AWS an on-premises file storage workload that depends on specific NetApp features ONTAP: storage efficiency via deduplication/compression, snapshots with quick restoration, snap-based replicationMirror and multiprotocol support (NFS and SMB) the same data set, with sub-milisecond latency for performance-sensitive applications (such as data banks via NFS). They want a fully managed file storage service at AWS that provides exactly the set of features and APIs of ONTAP, without restructuring the application to a different storage paradigm.
options: Use Amazon FSx for NetApp ONTAP
Use Amazon FSx for Lustre
Use Amazon FSx for Windows File Server
Use Amazon EFS (Elastic File System)
questions.explanation: Correct. Amazon FSx for NetApp ONTAP is a service fully managed by AWS running NetApp file system ONTAP real, providing native resources of the ONTAP (deduplication/compression for storage efficiency, Snapshots, SnapMirror replication, multiprotocol access NFS/SMB/iSCSI to the same data) with high performance and low latency storage — meeting directly the requirement to maintain the set of resources and APIs of ONTAP No restructuring.
questions.hint: The central requirement is to replicate exactly the capabilities of the NetApp file system ONTAP (SnapMirror, deduplication, multiprotocol) without restructuring the application — think about which FSx service runs its own ONTAP.
optionRationales: Correct. Amazon FSx for NetApp ONTAP is a service fully managed by AWS running NetApp file system ONTAP real, providing native resources of the ONTAP (deduplication/compression for storage efficiency, Snapshots, SnapMirror replication, multiprotocol access NFS/SMB/iSCSI to the same data) with high performance and low latency storage — meeting directly the requirement to maintain the set of resources and APIs of ONTAP No restructuring.

Incorrect. FSx for Windows File Server provides file storage based on SMB built on Windows Server, with native Windows resources (integration with Active Directory, ACLs NTFS, DFS), but DO NOT provide specific NetApp resources ONTAP, as SnapMirror replication or deduplication/multiprotocol in the format of ONTAP — is a different file system technology (based on Windows, not on ONTAP).

Incorrect. Amazon EFS is a file system NFS fully managed built on the distributed file technology of the AWS (not NetApp ONTAP); although support NFS and have its own backup/snapshot mechanisms, does not provide specific resources of ONTAP (SnapMirror, deduplication in style ONTAP, Multiprotocol NFS+SMB in the same volume in the sense of ONTAP) — would require restructuring in order to abandon specific dependencies of ONTAP.

Incorrect. FSx for Lustre is optimized for high performance computer workloads (HPC) and machine learning that require throughput/IOPS extremely high with a parallel file system (Lustre), strongly integrated with S3 for data processing pipelines — does not provide NetApp's enterprise resource set ONTAP (SnapMirror, deduplication in style ONTAP, support to SMB), making it inadequate for migration that depends on specific capacities of the ONTAP.

questions.text: A company is migrating a distributed database (Apache Cassandra style) to hundreds of instances EC2 within a single Availability Zone. The database design distributes replicas of each data partition between logical racks, and the company wants to minimize the chance that an underlying hardware failure (energy/shared network rack) affects multiple replicas of the same partition simultaneously. The solution needs to support hundreds of instances in the same AZ, grouped in line with the database's own replica distribution scheme..
options: Use a Cluster Placement Group to group all instances
Use a Partition Placement Group, distributing groups of instances (aligned to database replicas) between different logical partitions
Distribute multiple instances Auto Scaling Groups, one per Availability Zone, without using placement groups
Use a Spread Placement Group to ensure each instance is in distinct hardware
questions.explanation: Correct. A Partition Placement Group divides instances into logical partitions, each positioned in a distinct set of hardware racks (with separate power and network); instances within the same partition can share racks, but different partitions do not. 7 AZ partitions with hundreds of instances — ideal for systems like Cassandra, HDFS and Kafka, where you want to align hardware partitions to the replica distribution scheme of the distributed system itself.
questions.hint: Think about what kind of placement group allows you to group hundreds of instances into isolated hardware partitions, aligned to the replica scheme of a distributed system.
optionRationales: Correct. A Partition Placement Group divides instances into logical partitions, each positioned in a distinct set of hardware racks (with separate power and network); instances within the same partition can share racks, but different partitions do not. 7 AZ partitions with hundreds of instances — ideal for systems like Cassandra, HDFS and Kafka, where you want to align hardware partitions to the replica distribution scheme of the distributed system itself.

Incorrect. Cluster Placement Group groups the instances as close as possible to the same hardware, optimizing for ultra-low latency in strongly coupled loads (HPC) — exactly the OPOSTO of what is needed here (isolating fault domains), and increases the risk of a related hardware failure affecting many replicas simultaneously.

Incorrect. The Spread Placement Group places each instance in distinct hardware, without two instances sharing the same underlying hardware — but is limited to 7 AZ instances, not meeting the requirement of 'hundreds of instances' in the same AZ.

Incorrect. Trusting only in the distribution between AZs does not treat the isolation of rack/hardware failure level DENTRO of the same AZ, which is precisely what Partition Placement Groups provide; the scenario requires hundreds of instances in the same AZ with isolation aligned to replicas.

questions.text: A company operates a global distribution via Amazon CloudFront and, during the launch of a performance-sensitive product, needs almost real-time visibility (in the order of seconds) over metrics at the individual requisition level — latency, hit/miss cache, status code and edge location — for operational monitoring and alerts. CloudFront, delivered to Amazon S3, have delivery delay of up to several hours, which is inadequate for active monitoring during launch.
options: Enable Real-time Logs from CloudFront, configuring the delivery for the Amazon Kinesis Data Streams, and process with Kinesis Firehose Date/Lambda for dashboards and alerts almost in real time
Enable data events of AWS CloudTrail for the CloudFront, to capture data at the request level almost in real time
Use metrics of Amazon CloudWatch for the CloudFront, as a hit cache rate and total requests
Use standard access logs from CloudFront delivered to S3, consulting them with the Amazon Athena every few minutes
questions.explanation: The Real-time Logs of CloudFront deliver log data to Amazon Kinesis Data Streams in a seconds window, with sampling rate and configurable fields, allowing operational monitoring almost in real time — in sharp contrast to the time lag of standard log access.
questions.hint: The requirement is granularity by individual request delivered in seconds — think of what resource the CloudFront transmits flow logs instead of batch files.
optionRationales: The Real-time Logs of CloudFront deliver log data to Amazon Kinesis Data Streams in a seconds window, with sampling rate and configurable fields, allowing operational monitoring almost in real time — in sharp contrast to the time lag of standard log access.

Incorrect. Standard access logs have delivery latency typically up to 24 hours (frequently a few hours), which is inappropriate for the monitoring requirement almost in real time (seconds), regardless of the frequency of consultation.

Incorrect. CloudTrail capture management events/API (and, optionally, data events for some services), non-metric performance requirements content requirements of end users (latence, hit/miss cache) of distributions CloudFront — is not the appropriate mechanism for this use case.

Incorrect. CloudWatch for the CloudFront provide operational metrics AGREGADAS, with a granularity of not more than 1 minute, don't detail it. POR REQUIREMENT (individual ratio), edge location, specific status of each request) required for detailed operational analysis — Real-time Logs provide this granularity.

questions.text: A company needs to ingest clickstream data and deliver it, with the minimum operating overhead, directly to Amazon S3 in batches, with optional format conversion (JSON for Parquet) and compression, for further consultation with Amazon Athena. There is no need for customised real-time registration processing with sub-second latency by multiple independent consumer applications — only managed and reliable delivery to S3 with transformation.
options: Use Amazon Kinesis Data Streams with a custom consumer application (e.g. EC2) grouping batch records and recording them in S3
Use Amazon SQS to store in buffer the clickstream events, and an scheduled job of AWS Glue to read from SQS and record in S3
Use Amazon Kinesis Firehose data configured to deliver to S3 with format conversion for Parquet and compression
Use AWS DMS (Database Migration Service) to transmit the clickstream data to the S3
questions.explanation: Correct. Kinesis Data Firehose is a fully managed delivery service that stores in buffer, optionally transforms (format conversion, transformation via Lambda), compresses and delivers data to destinations as S3, Redshift and OpenSearch, without need to manage consumers/shards — meeting exactly the requirement of 'minimum operating overhead, delivery to S3 with transformation'.
questions.hint: Compare the level of management between the two services Kinesis: one requires building and operating consumer applications, the other delivers directly to destinations with integrated transformation.
optionRationales: Correct. Kinesis Data Firehose is a fully managed delivery service that stores in buffer, optionally transforms (format conversion, transformation via Lambda), compresses and delivers data to destinations as S3, Redshift and OpenSearch, without need to manage consumers/shards — meeting exactly the requirement of 'minimum operating overhead, delivery to S3 with transformation'.

Incorrect. Data Streams requires to build and manage custom consumer applications (by dealing with iterators shard, checkpointing, scaling and format conversion logic) — operational overhead significantly higher than Firehose for the simple requirement to deliver to S3 with transformation'; Data Streams is the right choice when you need customised real-time MULTIPLES consumers with sub-second access to the raw stream.

Incorrect. SQS is a general-purpose message row, not designed for high throughput streaming intake with ordination/replay semantics, and has no native format/compression conversion in delivery to S3 — this pipeline would be much more complex and customized than Firehose, which has already been designed for this purpose..

Incorrect. DMS is designed to migrate/replicate data from BANCOS OF DADOS (using CDC) for destinations, not for ingesting data from EVENTOS clickstream generated by applications — is not the appropriate service for this case of using streaming intake.

questions.text: A function AWS Lambda which sustains a API the customer has peaks of latency by cold start during a daily increase of traffic that starts precisely at 9h e ends at 18h (commercial schedule, predictable standard). The team configured Provisioned Competition to eliminate cold starts during this window, but does not want to pay for this provided competition 24 hours per day — it should be automatically increased before 9h and reduced after 18h, on a recurring daily schedule.
options: Set Reserved Competition in function to match expected peak traffic, activate all the time
Use AWS Implementation Auto Scaling with a scheduled scaling action (scheduled scaling) directed to the Provisioned Competition configuration of the function Lambda (for a published version/alias)
Configure target tracking policies based on the CompetitiveExecutions metric CloudWatch
Increase function memory allocation Lambda, which increases proportionally to CPU and reduces the duration of the cold start
questions.explanation: Correct. The Application Auto Scaling Supports Provided Competition from Lambda as a 'scalable target', and scheduled scaling actions allow you to set recurring schedules (based on cron) to increase/reduce the Provided Competition set at specific times — taking exactly into account the predictable daily business schedule pattern, avoiding paying for provided competition outside this window.
questions.hint: The traffic pattern is completely predictable per hour — think of what mechanism allows pre-provisioning and then reduce competition from Lambda in scheduled times, instead of reacting to demand.
optionRationales: Correct. The Application Auto Scaling Supports Provided Competition from Lambda as a 'scalable target', and scheduled scaling actions allow you to set recurring schedules (based on cron) to increase/reduce the Provided Competition set at specific times — taking exactly into account the predictable daily business schedule pattern, avoiding paying for provided competition outside this window.

Incorrect. Target tracking reacts to metric/use changes ATUAL (This would still allow the occurrence of cold start-ups while competition is increased reactively at the beginning of the increase in traffic; for a time frame, the CONHECIDO e PREVIOUS, scheduled phasing pre-provisions competition ANTES from the beginning of the peak, completely avoiding the cold start.

Incorrect. Increasing memory can reduce the duration of a cold start to a certain point, but not ELIMINA cold startups, and does not meet the cost optimization objective of having provided competition only during business hours — is a lever unrelated to the requirement.

Incorrect. Reserved Competition limits/guaranteed the allocation of competition, but does NOT pre-initiate running environments (does not eliminate cold startups) — that is specifically what Provided Competition does; moreover, setting it permanently at peak level does not meet the requirement to reduce outside business hours.

questions.text: A production database Amazon RDS for PostgreSQL presents intermittent performance degradation. The DBA team needs to identify which consultations SQL specific, waiting events (wait events) or database load (in terms of Average Active Sessions) are responsible during these degradation windows, with minimal configuration, ideally with a visual dashboard showing the database load detailed by SQL, wait state, user and host over time, including historical data retained for at least one week without additional infrastructure.
options: Enable Amazon RDS Performance Insights
Enable Enhanced Monitoring in the instance RDS to visualize metrics at the level of the operating system with granularity of 1 second
Configure a separate dashboard in Amazon CloudWatch with custom metrics published by a script that consults pg_stat_statements periodically
Enable Slow Queries log RDS and analyze the logs with the Amazon Athena
questions.explanation: Correct. Performance Insights is a fully managed database performance monitoring feature that provides a database load dashboard (DB Load, measured in Average Active Sessions)/AAS), with the ability to detail the load by query SQL, wait event, user, host and other dimensions; retains performance data by 7 days without additional cost (longer retention in paid layer), no need to install agents or manage additional infrastructure.
questions.hint: Think of what native resource of RDS provides a database load dashboard (Average Active Sessions) detailed by SQL and wait event, without agents or additional infrastructure.
optionRationales: Correct. Performance Insights is a fully managed database performance monitoring feature that provides a database load dashboard (DB Load, measured in Average Active Sessions)/AAS), with the ability to detail the load by query SQL, wait event, user, host and other dimensions; retains performance data by 7 days without additional cost (longer retention in paid layer), no need to install agents or manage additional infrastructure.

Incorrect. Enhanced Monitoring provides metrics at the level of SISTEMA OPERACIONAL (CPU, memory, disk, network at the underlying host level, via agent), not analysis at the level of BANCO OF DADOS of consultations SQL/wait events — it is complementary, but does not answer 'what consultations SQL/Wait events are causing the load'.

Incorrect. This approach requires building and maintaining custom scripts/infrastructures to extract and publish data from pg_stat_statements, something that Performance Insights already natively provides as a managed resource with integrated visual dashboard — far greater operational overhead for the same result.

Incorrect. Slow query logs capture queries that exceed a limit, but do not provide the holistic and real-time view of 'Average Active Sessions detailed by wait event/SQL/user, and analyze via Athena requires exporting logs and building queries — a much more manual and less integrated approach than the native dashboard of Performance Insights.

questions.text: A company operates a transactional database Amazon RDS for MySQL (db.r6g.xlarge) that supports an application OLTP. The Business Intelligence team wants to perform long-term, heavy analytical consultations on the same data, but these consultations currently consume resources and degrade the application performance OLTP when performed in the primary instance. Reporting queries do not need to run in the same class of the primary instance (they are less sensitive in time and can tolerate replication/consistency lag if possible), but EXIGEM CPU/substantial memory for complex aggregations over a larger volume of data.
options: Increase the class of instance from the primary to a larger size, so as to accommodate both the workload OLTP the number of reports
Create a Read Replica Amazon RDS with a class of instance MAIOR (or more optimized for memory/CPU) than the primary, and direct the IB/report consultations to this read reply
Use the standby instance of the Multi-AZ of Amazon RDS to execute the report queries (since it is a copy of the primary)
Migrate the entire database to the Amazon Redshift, to meet both the workload OLTP the analytical
questions.explanation: Right. The Read Replicas of RDS can use a class of instance DIFERENTE of origin/primary, allowing to dimension the replica appropriately to the resource needs of the report load (independent of the dimensioning) OLTP of the primary), while fully removing the analytical load from the primary, which continues to attend traffic OLTP without containment; replication lag is an acceptable trade-off for reports, as required.
questions.hint: Think about which property of the Read Replicas RDS allows them to be dimensioned independently of the primary instance for reading workloads with different resource requirements.
optionRationales: Right. The Read Replicas of RDS can use a class of instance DIFERENTE of origin/primary, allowing to dimension the replica appropriately to the resource needs of the report load (independent of the dimensioning) OLTP of the primary), while fully removing the analytical load from the primary, which continues to attend traffic OLTP without containment; replication lag is an acceptable trade-off for reports, as required.

Incorrect. Increasing the PRIMARY instance to support both workloads still means that report queries will compete with transactions OLTP by resources in the MESMA instance (CPU, I/O, buffer pool), causing restraint regardless of the size of the instance; a separate read replica isolates the workloads.

Incorrect. STANDBY Multi-AZ is not accessible for reading queries (it exists exclusively for failover, using synchronous replication for high availability, not for downloading readings) — this differs from a Read Replica, which is consultable; trying to consult the standby is not a supported standard.

Incorrect. Redshift is a data warehouse OLAP columnar, not optimized for workloads OLTP transactional (line-to-line inserts/updates, short transactions of high competition) — migrate TODO the bank OLTP for the Redshift would be inadequate for the transactional needs of the application; a response directed to the reports is a much smaller and less disruptive change.

questions.text: One API REST built on Amazon API Gateway + AWS Lambda exposes the endpoint 'GET /products/{id}', called with very high frequency for the same product IDs, with product data changing only a few times a day. Lambda consults the database and moderately costly calculations, and the team wants to reduce both the number of invocations of the Lambda (cost) as to the response latency for repeated requests of the same product ID, without building a separate cache layer (such as ElastiCache) and without changing the logic of the function Lambda.
options: Enable cache of API Gateway in the stage of API REST, configuring a TTL appropriate for the frequency of change of product data
Increase the reserved competition of the function Lambda to deal with more simultaneous requests for the same product ID more efficiently
Implant Amazon ElastiCache for Redis and modify the function Lambda to check the cache before the database
Implement cache logic within function Lambda using a dictionary in memory that persists between invocations through the reuse of the execution context
questions.explanation: Correct. The retention settings of the CloudWatch Logs automatically and permanently delete log events older than the configured retention period, directly reducing the volume of stored log data (and associated storage costs) over time, while retaining a defined window of recent logs for debugging — this can be configured by log group (manually, via CLI/IAC, or in mass, saw a script that iterated on the log groups).

questions.text: A company uses AWS Step Functions Standard Workflows to orchestrate a high volume and short-duration data processing pipeline, invoked millions of times a day, with each execution ending in less than a few seconds (e.g. transformation/validation by event triggered by requests for API). They realize that the costs of Step Functions (in the Standard Workflows) have become a significant expense given the volume of MILHIONES of daily and short executions, even though for this specific workflow, resources of the Standard Workflows as a retention of execution history of up to 90 days or semantics of execution exactly-once.

questions.explanation: Correct. Express Workflows are precised based on the NUMBER OF EXECUTIONS, their DURATION and memory consumption (similar to the model of precification of the Lambda), instead of by transition of status as in Standard Workflows — for workflows of ALTO VOLUME and CURTA DURATION (millions of short runs), Express Workflows are significantly more economical; the trade-off is execution 'at-last-once' (instead of 'exactly-once' of the Standard) and retention of shorter execution history (based on CloudWatch Logs, not in the complete history of the console of Step Functions) — acceptable for this case of use of high volume and short duration that does not depend on these specific guarantees of the Standard.
questions.hint: Workflow has millions of short runs per day and does not depend on exact-once guarantees or long-term execution history — think of what kind of Step Functions has a precision model based on execution/duration instead of by state transition.
optionRationales: Correct. Express Workflows are precised based on the NUMBER OF EXECUTIONS, their DURATION and memory consumption (similar to the model of precification of the Lambda), instead of by transition of status as in Standard Workflows — for workflows of ALTO VOLUME and CURTA DURATION (millions of short runs), Express Workflows are significantly more economical; the trade-off is execution 'at-last-once' (instead of 'exactly-once' of the Standard) and retention of shorter execution history (based on CloudWatch Logs, not in the complete history of the console of Step Functions) — acceptable for this case of use of high volume and short duration that does not depend on these specific guarantees of the Standard.

Incorrect. Remove Step Functions would completely eliminate orchestration costs, but also remove the BENEFITS from using the Step Functions (visual definition of workflow, integrated error/retries treatment, state management) — this is a much more invasive architectural change than simply changing the TIPO of workflow within the Step Functions, which directly deals with the cost problem per state transition to this execution profile.

Incorrect. Reducing the number of states could reduce the cost per execution a little (less transitions = lower cost per execution under the standard's transitional precision), but it does not fundamentally change the MODELO PRECIFICATION — For millions of daily executions, the precision model based on the execution of the Express Workflows is fundamentally more appropriate, regardless of how many states remain, without requiring a redesign of the logic of the workflow.

Incorrect. Batching could reduce the number of runs, but introduces LATENCY (waiting to accumulate a batch) for workflows described as ending 'in less than a few seconds' per event (i.e., event processing is desired) — and adds complexity to the batch division logic within the workflow; moving to Express Workflows addresses the cost problem directly without changing the execution model per event.

questions.text: A company stores user-generated content (photos and documents) in a Amazon S3. questions.explanation: Correct. S3 Intelligent-Tiering monitors the access patterns of each object individually and moves it automatically between access levels (without performance impact and no recovery rate between Frequent and Infrequent Access), charging only a small rate of monitoring per object. This resolves exactly the scenario of unpredictable and uncorrelated access patterns with the age of the object, eliminating the need for age-based life-cycle rules.
questions.hint: Think of what mechanism the S3 monitors the actual access behavior of each object, instead of assuming that age predicts the frequency of use.
optionRationales: Correct. This resolves exactly the scenario of unpredictable and uncorrelated access patterns with the age of the object, eliminating the need for age-based life-cycle rules.

Incorrect. Age-based life-cycle rules presuppose a correlation between age and access frequency (older objects would be less accessed). The scenario explicitly states that this correlation does NOT exist — an object can remain popular for months (generating AI recovery rates) or become cold immediately (staying in Standard without need until the 30 This violates the optimization requirement based on actual access pattern, not age.

Incorrect. S3 One Zone-IA reduces the storage cost by storing data in a single Availability Zone (with durability trade-off), but does not solve the optimization based on the default of ACESSO described in the scenario – in addition, it also charges recovery fees like Standard-IA, which would penalize frequently accessed objects.

questions.text: A company operates several bodies of the Amazon RDS for PostgreSQL and Amazon Aurora MySQL using instance classes based on Intel processors (db.m5 and db.r5). questions.text: A company has a function AWS Lambda performing an intensive data transformation in CPU and memory. questions.text: A company operates 10 independent microservices, each behind its own Application Load Balancer dedicated, all in the same VPC and attending traffic to the same domain (different paths or subdomains per service, ex.: api.example.com/orders, api.example.com/stock). Weighted routing distributes traffic PROPORCIONALMENTE between multiple endpoints (e.g. for canary implantations or load distribution between IDENTICAL backends), but not REDUZ the number of ALBs (all 10 would continue to exist and generate collections) — and is not designed to ROTEAR Requirements DIFERENTES for SERVICES DIFERENTES based on path/host (this is content based router, not weighted distribution)).

questions.text: A company uses the Amazon EFS (General Purpose performance mode) as shared file system, accessed by an application in multiple instances EC2. This would require that the APPLICATION be modified to determine, MOMENTO GRAVATION, which file system to use based on an access frequency PREVISTA (this scenario suggests not to be known reliably in advance, since the access pattern emerges over time). questions.text: A company has several instances EC2 running application code that makes POLLING CONTINUED in one API external, database table or pocket S3 every few seconds, 24 hours a day, looking for new items to process — even if new items arrive sporadically (sometimes with interval hours). Redesign the architecture for an event-oriented model: configure the source (e.g. event notifications from S3, DynamoDB Streams, or an scheduled/disposed mechanism for external APIs) to send events to a row Amazon SQS (or shoot directly at AWS Lambda), and use a function AWS Lambda driven by the queue/event/stream to perform the processing.

Incorrect. Move the polling logic to DENTRO from the database (via scheduled job) does not eliminate the continuous consumption of resources — just transfer ONDE the continuous polling occurs (of EC2 for the database engine), and instances RDS they also generate continuous computer charges; it does not reach the event-oriented model, with payment only during processing, which SQS+Lambda offers.

questions.text: A company executes a batch-tolerant and horizontally scalable batch processing load using instances EC2 Spot within a Auto Scaling The team observed that when the AWS recovers capacity Spot, the standard warning of interruption of 2 minutes sometimes is not enough for the tasks in progress to be completed cleanly and for the replacement capacity to be launched and become healthy, causing small processing gaps and occasionally loss of work. PROATIVAMENTE cases Spot with high risk of interruption ANTES even from the warning of 2 minutes be issued, gaining more time for graceful treatment and replacement, maintaining the use of Spot for cost-saving.

questions.text: A company has enabled the Amazon S3 Transfer Acceleration in a pocket used by an application whose customers (instances EC2 and on-premises servers connected via AWS Direct Connect) are TODOS localized in MESMA Region AWS After enabling the Transfer Acceleration, the team perceives a AUMENTO in the costs of data upload, without any measurable improvement in the speed of transfer to these customers who are already in the same region. questions.text: A company uses AWS Backup to create daily backups of your volumes Amazon EBS and databases Amazon RDS, withheld by regulatory requirement of compliance by 7 years. Currently, all backups remain at the standard (hot) storage level of the AWS Backup throughout the retention period of 7 years, which is costly given the accumulated volume of backups. Backups with more than 90 days are virtually never restored (only ~90 more recent days are effectively used for recovery), but they need to remain recoverable (being acceptable a recovery time of several hours) throughout the entire compliance period of 7 years.
options: Switch daily backups to weekly backups for volumes/databanks with more than 90 days, reducing the number of recovery points stored.
Reduce retention period of backups from 7 years to 90 days to reduce storage cost.
Copy, via custom script, backups with more than 90 days for a bucket from Amazon S3 Glacier Deep Archive and delete them from AWS Backup.
Configure life cycle definitions of the plan AWS Backup to transition recovery points to the cold storage level after 90 days, keeping the total retention of 7 years.
questions.explanation: Correct. Cold storage level of the AWS Backup offers storage cost per GB significantly lower than standard (hot) storage while still meeting the multi-hour recovery time considered acceptable for the oldest rarely needed backups — and the AWS Backup imposes a minimum period of 90 days in cold storage before deletion. This directly aligns the storage cost to the actual recovery time target of the old backups, maintaining the regulatory requirement of retention of 7 years.
questions.hint: Think of a native resource of AWS Backup that moves older recovery points to a cheaper storage level without removing them from the backup catalog.
optionRationales: Correct. Cold storage level of the AWS Backup offers storage cost per GB significantly lower than standard (hot) storage while still meeting the multi-hour recovery time considered acceptable for the oldest rarely needed backups — and the AWS Backup imposes a minimum period of 90 days in cold storage before deletion. This directly aligns the storage cost to the actual recovery time target of the old backups, maintaining the regulatory requirement of retention of 7 years.

Incorrect. Reduce retention below regulatory requirement (7 years) would create a COMPLIANCE; the scenario explicitly states that the retention of 7 years is a regulatory requirement and cannot simply be reduced to reduce costs.

Incorrect. This would require building and maintaining a process CUSTOMIZADO export/migration out of native life cycle management of AWS Backup, and remove those backups from the unified recovery point/restore flow catalog of AWS Backup — the native transition to cold storage AWS Backup achieves cost reduction without custom tools and without losing the unified backup management interface.

Incorrect. Change backup frequency to data ANTIGOS does not make sense (backups already exist; it is not possible to retroactively reduce the frequency of past backups), and reduce the future frequency does not solve the CUSTO THE LEVEL OF ARMAZENAMENTO of the already accumulated backups, which is the cost factor described — is a different (and partially inconsistent) lever than is being requested.

questions.text: A company maintains separate environments from Amazon RDS for MySQL for production, staging and development. The three environments are currently configured with Multi-AZ implementations (synchronous standby replica in a second AZ), configured uniformly via a template of the CloudFormation shared 'by consistency'. The staging and development environments are used only during the commercial time for tests and are NOT subject to the same SLAs of production availability — a brief unavailability during a maintenance window or instance failure in these environments is acceptable and does not impact customers. The team wants to reduce the costs of the RDS for staging and development without affecting the position of production availability.
options: Disable Multi-AZ for instances RDS of staging and development, keeping the Multi-AZ enabled for production.
Configure instances RDS staging and development to automatically stop off business hours, keeping Multi-AZ enabled during the hours in which they are running.
Use Reserved Instances of the RDS for the staging and development databases to reduce the cost of Multi-AZ.
Migrate the staging and development databases to Amazon Aurora Serverless v2, maintaining Multi-AZ, to reduce costs.
questions.explanation: Correct. Multi-AZ deployments approximately double the cost of the instance RDS (running and replicating synchronously to a standby in a second AZ) to provide automatic failover for ALTA DISPONIBILIDADE; as staging and development explicitly do not require the same SLA production availability (short availability is acceptable), disable Multi-AZ in these non-productive environments removes the cost of the standby instance, while production maintains its Multi-AZ protection — aligning directly the infrastructure configuration to the actual requirement of availability of each environment.
questions.hint: Think about which configuration of the RDS approximately doubles the cost of the instance to provide a level of availability that non-productive environments may not need.
optionRationales: Correct. Multi-AZ deployments approximately double the cost of the instance RDS (running and replicating synchronously to a standby in a second AZ) to provide automatic failover for ALTA DISPONIBILIDADE; as staging and development explicitly do not require the same SLA production availability (short availability is acceptable), disable Multi-AZ in these non-productive environments removes the cost of the standby instance, while production maintains its Multi-AZ protection — aligning directly the infrastructure configuration to the actual requirement of availability of each environment.

Incorrect. Aurora Serverless v2 SUPORTA Multi-AZ, but this introduces a MIGRATION OF ENGINE of database (of RDS for MySQL for Aurora MySQL) as a cost reduction mechanism, which is a much larger change (compatibility tests, migration effort) than simply disable Multi-AZ in the existing engine — and KEEP Multi-AZ (the cost factor identified) instead of removing it to environments that do not need it.

Incorrect. Reserved Instances offer a discount on the invoice on the contracted instance configuration, but do not eliminate the fundamental duplication of resources that the Multi-AZ requires (the reservation would cover both the primary instance and QUANTO the standby, with discount, but still paying for two instances) — reduces the cost partially, but does not resolve the root inefficiency of maintaining unnecessary standby replicas for environments that do not need high availability.

Incorrect. Stop instances outside business hours REDUZ some cost (no computer charge while stopping), but instances RDS Multi-AZ continue to incur the duplicate cost (primary + standby) during the hours when they are running, which is precisely when the unnecessary cost of high availability occurs — it is a complementary optimization (reducing run-times), but does not resolve the multi-AZ configuration breakdown itself.

questions.text: A company operates a table of Amazon DynamoDB in Provisioned Capacity Mode, with Read Capacity Units (RCUs) and Write Capacity Units (WCUs) configured based on initial estimates made over a year ago, without Auto Scaling set up. The team suspects that the capacity provided today is significantly above the required (super-provided), resulting in unnecessary cost, but wants CONFIRMAR this with DADOS before reducing the provided values, to avoid causing throttling if the reduction is very aggressive.
options: Reduce RCUs and WCUs provided in 50% immediately as a quick first step, monitoring the throttling after.
Enable DynamoDB Accelerator (DAX) in front of the table to reduce the reading capacity required.
Change the table immediately to On-Demand capacity mode of the DynamoDB, which automatically charges only for actual use.

Analyze the metrics of the Amazon CloudWatch ConsumedReadCapacityUnits and ConsumedWriteCapacityUnits of the table over a representative period (including peaks), compare with currently provided RCUs/WCUs, adjust the provided capacity to align with observed peak consumption (plus one margin) and/or enable the DynamoDB Auto Scaling.
questions.explanation: Correct. Using the actual ConsumedCapacity metrics provides the data-oriented base to correctly dimension the provided capacity without guessing, avoiding directly both over-supply (spent cost) and under-supply (throttling) — and enable the Auto Scaling from front to front automatically adjusts capacity within defined limits based on real traffic.
questions.hint: Think of what metrics of CloudWatch reveal consumption REAL of a table capacity DynamoDB, allowing comparison with what is provided before any change.
optionRationales: Correct. Using the actual ConsumedCapacity metrics provides the data-oriented base to correctly dimension the provided capacity without guessing, avoiding directly both over-supply (spent cost) and under-supply (throttling) — and enable the Auto Scaling from front to front automatically adjusts capacity within defined limits based on real traffic.

Incorrect. On-Demand mode It is a valid alternative that removes the need to manage provided capacity, but for a table with STABLE and PREVIOUS traffic (what the analysis of Consumed metrics would reveal), the provided capacity (especially with Reserved Capacity or Auto Scaling) It's usually SIGNIFICATIVAMENTE MAIS BARATA by request than On-Demand — moving to On-Demand without first analyzing the consumption pattern (the scenario asks 'confirm with data before') ignores the analysis stage and may not be the most economical choice for stable workloads.

Incorrect. Reduce capacity PRIMEIRO and monitor throttling DEPOIS is a reactive and risky approach that can cause throttling/errors in production for end users before the team perceives and corrects — the scenario explicitly asks 'confirm with data ANTES to reduce', i.e. the analysis should precede the change of capacity, not follow.

Incorrect. DAX is a cache layer in memory that can reduce the load of LEITURA that reaches the table DynamoDB for intense reading workloads with repeatedly accessed items, but ADICIONA its own infrastructure cost (the cluster us) DAX) and does not directly answer the question of whether the values ATUAIS of RCU/WCU provided are already over-provided in relation to real demand — it is a different optimization (cache), not the correct dimensioning of the provided capacity based on consumption data.

questions.text: A company has a data center on-premises that transfers approximately 50 TB Data POR MONTHS for the Amazon S3 through a connection VPN based on the internet, incurring substantial data transfer charges from AWS for on-premises (and the internet connection occasionally becomes a gargalo during peak transfer windows). This transfer volume should remain stable or grow. The team wants to reduce the costs per GB of this consistent and high volume hybrid connectivity, also improving the transfer reliability/throughput.
options: Enable S3 Transfer Acceleration in destination bucks to accelerate and reduce the cost of uploads coming from on-premises.
Establish a connection AWS Direct Connect between the data center on-premises and the AWS.

questions.explanation: Correct. Direct Connect provides a dedicated network connection with data transfer fees SAID significantly MENORES by GB than standard Internet transfer rates, besides providing more consistent network throughput and less latency than a VPN internet-based — for a standard of hybrid transfer ALTO VOLUME (50 TB/month), the reduced price of exit via Direct Connect typically generates substantial economy compared to Internet output, besides improved reliability/throughput.
questions.hint: Think about what kind of dedicated connection between on-premises and AWS is designed to reduce the cost per GB of recurrent and high volume output transfers.
optionRationales: Correct. Direct Connect provides a dedicated network connection with data transfer fees SAID significantly MENORES by GB than standard Internet transfer rates, besides providing more consistent network throughput and less latency than a VPN internet-based — for a standard of hybrid transfer ALTO VOLUME (50 TB/month), the reduced price of exit via Direct Connect typically generates substantial economy compared to Internet output, besides improved reliability/throughput.

Incorrect. Transfer Acceleration optimizes speed UPLOAD for the S3 via edge locations of the CloudFront (for data entering the AWS), but the cost concern of the scenario is about data transfer from AWS for on-premises — the Transfer Acceleration does not apply or reduce costs of exit transfer (egress), and it adds its own fee for input transfers that accelerate.

Incorrect. The cost concern described is about the costs of TRANSFER OF DADOS (egress) for a recurrent flow of 50 TB/month, not about the cost of ARMAZENAMENTO of data S3 — move the data to the Glacier first would add time/recovery rates before even the transfer could occur, and does not address the price of the output transfer by GB at all.

Incorrect. Snowball is designed for single mass transfers, or INFREQUENTES (e.g. initial migrations), where the volume of data makes the transfer via network impractical; use it in a database MENSAL RECORRENTE for the continuous operating flow introduces a significant operating overload (device logistics, handling) compared to a link. Direct Connect persistent, which is designed exactly for sustained and recurrent hybrid connectivity with lower cost per GB.

questions.text: A company owns a Amazon S3 containing 200 millions of existing objects, accumulated over several years, all currently in the storage class S3 Standard. The team determined (via S3 Storage Class Analysis) that most of these objects EXISTENTES should be moved to the S3 Flexible Retrieval Glacier to reduce costs. However, life cycle rules of S3 based on age of the object are applied considering the date of CREATION of each object from the creation of the rule — for objects that are already above the desired age threshold, the team wants the transition to be applied to objects EXISTENTES controlled, traceable and RETROATIVA, instead of depending on the time of assessment of life-cycle rules for objects that already exceed the threshold.
options: Use command `aws s3 cp AWS CLI with the flags `--recursive` and `--storage-class` to copy each object over itself with the new storage class.

Use Amazon S3 Batch Operations with a storage class copy/change job to retroactively apply the transition to S3 Flexible Glacier Retrieval to 200 millions of existing objects based on a manifest (e.g. via S3 Inventory).

questions.explanation: Correct. S3 Batch Operations was specifically designed to perform a specified operation (including storage class transitions) in a large, defined list of objects EXISTENTES, in a single traceable job (with completion reports), providing a controlled and auditable mechanism for retroactively trading existing objects — separated from (and complementing a) continuous Lifecycle rules dealing with objects NOVOS from now on.
questions.hint: Think of what resource the S3 was designed to perform a mass operation, traceable and with completion report, on a list of existing objects.
optionRationales: Correct. S3 Batch Operations was specifically designed to perform a specified operation (including storage class transitions) in a large, defined list of objects EXISTENTES, in a single traceable job (with completion reports), providing a controlled and auditable mechanism for retroactively trading existing objects — separated from (and complementing a) continuous Lifecycle rules dealing with objects NOVOS from now on.

Incorrect. Although Lifecycle rules of the S3 SE APLIQUEM existing objects that already meet the age criterion (the S3 evaluates and transitions, usually around a day after the rule is created, not instantly), the scenario specifically asks for a process CONTROLADO AND RATREAVABLE FOR 200 millions of objects — the evaluation of Lifecycle rules for a massive backlog of existing objects does not provide the same level of conclusion/trace/grain retry report as a dedicated job of S3 Batch Operations, which is the approach recommended by AWS for large-scale retroactive operations.

Incorrect. Although technically that PUDESSE change the storage class via copy operation, execute this against 200 millions of objects via CLI would be extremely slow (sequential/limited parallelism), does not have the mechanisms of job tracking/conclusion reports/retry of S3 Batch Operations, and it is not a scalable or recommended approach by AWS for operations on this scale.

Incorrect. Enable Intelligent-Tiering as a storage class for objects NOVOS does not retroactively alter the storage class of objects EXISTENTES already stored as S3 Standard — Intelligent-Tiering needs to be explicitly DEFINIDO as the storage class of the objects (existing objects maintain their current class unless explicitly transitioned), so this does not solve the declared need to migrate 200 millions of existing Standard objects.

questions.text: A company operates a cluster Amazon Redshift for its production data warehouse, used by the analysis team. In addition to the production cluster, the team maintains a cluster Redshift separate used exclusively for the development/test of new pipelines from ETL and consultations — this dev/test cluster is used actively only during business hours on working days (approximately 50 of the 168 hours of the week), but currently it rotates continuously, generating computer charges 24/7. The team wants to reduce the cost of computing this dev/test cluster during the ~118 weekly hours in which it gets idle, without losing the cluster configuration, the data loaded, or having to recreate it at a time.
options: Use pause and summary functionality of Amazon Redshift for PAUSAR the dev/test cluster during the ~118 weekly hours without use (for example, I saw an action scheduled to pause at the end of the day and resume every morning)).

Migrate the dev/test workload to Amazon Redshift Serverless, which charges only when queries are running, eliminating the need for cluster scheduling.
questions.explanation: Right, while a cluster Redshift is paused, the computer collections (us) PARAM to be generated (only storage charges continue), and the configuration, data and endpoint of the cluster are PRESERVADOS for when it is resumed — directly eliminating the cost of computing during idle periods without losing configuration or data, and this can be automated via scheduled actions of Redshift.
questions.hint: Think of a functionality of Redshift which interrupts the computer collection while preserving the configuration and data of the cluster, without requiring re-creation or endpoint change.
optionRationales: Right, while a cluster Redshift is paused, the computer collections (us) PARAM to be generated (only storage charges continue), and the configuration, data and endpoint of the cluster are PRESERVADOS for when it is resumed — directly eliminating the cost of computing during idle periods without losing configuration or data, and this can be automated via scheduled actions of Redshift.

Incorrect. Resize for us smaller reduces the rate POR HORA, But it doesn't solve the fact that ~118 of the 168 weekly hours ZERO active use — pay a reduced rate per 168 hours is still more than paying the full fee for just the ~50 hours really needed; is an incremental reduction, not the elimination of idle time cost.

Incorrect. Delete and restore from snapshot PARA the computer charges during the 'excluded' period (cost benefit similar to the pause), but restoring a cluster from a snapshot is a very MAIS LENTA (potentially dozens of minutes to hours, depending on the volume of data) compared to resuming a paused cluster (typically faster), and the ENDPOINT cluster changes after restoration (requiring connection string update) — pause/summary preserves the endpoint and is the least overloaded native mechanism for exactly this use case.

Incorrect. Redshift Serverless is a valid payment-by-use alternative, but migrate the dev/test workload from a cluster PROVISIONADO existing for Serverless is a wider MUDANÇA (different collection/configuration model, based on RPUs, possible differences in query performance characteristics) than simply enable pause/summary scheduling in the cluster EXISTENTE — pause/summary is the direct and minimal change solution to the idle time cost problem described in an existing provided cluster.

C) Incorrect: crawler catalog metadata; does not control what the job has already processed. D) Incorrect: versioning protects objects against overwritten; does not influence the scope of the job.

questions.text: A stream of the Kinesis Data Streams has 5 consumer applications. With standard shared consumption, consumers compete for 2 MB/s reading per shard and delivery latency increased. The requirement is that CADA consumer has dedicated reading throughput and delivery latency of ~70 ms, without increasing the number of shards. Which feature answers?
options: Migrate consumers to long polling

C) Incorrect: minor batch can even increase overload; does not create dedicated throughput. D) Incorrect: retention affects how long data can be reread, not throughput.

questions.text: Intermittently slow requirements cross: CloudFront → API Gateway → Lambda A → Lambda B → DynamoDB. questions.text: A payment company needs to perform cryptographic operations (signature and encryption) with keys that, by contract, must reside in HSMs of single tenant under its sole control, but wants very high availability of such operations within the VPC. One single Auto Scaling Group covering the two regions
questions.explanation: (a) Correct: or Route 53 directs users to the nearest/healthy region and takes a region from the air automatically via health checks. B) Incorrect: ALBs are regional — does not exist ALB between regions. C) Correct: the data layer needs multi-region replication native (Global Tables)/Aurora Global). D) Incorrect: peering connects networks; does not distribute users or replicates data. E) Correct: each Region needs its complete and independent computer stack. F) Incorrect: a ASG does not cross regions — it is a regional resource.

questions.text: A site behind the CloudFront + ALB is suffering from layer attacks 7: Requisition floods HTTP of thousands of IPs and attempts to SQL injection. DUAS measures mitigate these attacks on the edge? (Select DUAS alternatives)
options: Linking AWS WAF to distribution, with managed rules (SQLi)/XSS) and rate-based rules against flood
Increase the size of the origin instances
Move the origin to another region
Hire AWS Shield Advanced for managed DDoS protection, visibility and support SRT
Lock the door 443 no Security Group of origin
questions.explanation: (a) Correct: or WAF filter malicious patterns (managed rules) and rate-based rules automatically limit abusive IPs — everything on the edge, before the origin. B) Incorrect: scaling the origin absorbs more attack rather than blocking it — and expensive. C) Incorrect: changing the region does not affect attacks that follow the DNS. D) Correct: or Shield Advanced adds advanced DDoS detection/mitigation (L3/L4/L7), Shield Response Team and cost protection. E) Incorrect: block 443 knock down the website itself.

questions.text: The consultations of the Amazon Athena about a data lake of logs in JSON are expensive (scanned data collection) and slow. DUAS Do optimizations drastically reduce the volume scanned per query? (Select DUAS alternatives)
options: Convert data to compressed columnal format (Apache Parquet)/ORC)
Increase the number of bucks S3
Share data by date (e.g. year/month/day) and filter by partitions in queries
Migrate consultations to the same SQL no RDS
Enable MFA Delete No Bucket
questions.explanation: A) Correct: column format allows you to read only the columns used in the query, with compression — reductions in 90%+ in scanning are common. B) Incorrect: the amount of buckets does not influence the volume scanned by query. C) Correct: with Hive style partitioning + filter WHERE in the partition, the Athena read only the relevant folders (partition pruning). D) Incorrect: move data lake logs to a bank OLTP Inverts architecture and multiplies costs.: MFA Delete is protection against exclusion, no effect in consultation.

questions.text: Functions Lambda associated with a VPC need: (1) consult a bank RDS in private sub-network, and (2) call one API public third party on the internet. Today internet calls fail by timeout. DUAS settings fix architecture? (Select DUAS alternatives)
options: Provide one NAT Gateway in a public sub-network of VPC
Link an Elastic IP directly to the function Lambda
Add route 0.0.0.0/0 → NAT Gateway on the road table of the private sub-networks used by the Lambda
Move function Lambda for the public sub-network with automatic IP
Create a Gateway Endpoint for the API of third parties
questions.explanation: A) Correct: Internet access from private sub-networks requires a NAT Gateway (B) Incorrect: it is not possible to attach Elastic IP to a function Lambda. C) Correct: without the default route pointing to the NAT, Internet traffic has no way — the two pieces (NAT + D) Incorrect: Lambdas in VPC use ENIs that do not receive public IP — public sub-network does not resolve. S3 and DynamoDB, not for external APIs.

questions.text: A table of the DynamoDB that stores events uses the date (YYYY-MM-DD) as partition key and undergoes throttling at peak times, even with aggregate capacity remaining. DUAS design techniques correct this hot partition? (Select DUAS alternatives)
options: Exchange the partition key for an attribute of ALTA cardinality and uniform access (e.g. device/user ID))
Increase the average size of items
Apply write sharding: add a calculated suffix to the key (e.g. date)#1..date#N) to spread the same day's writings between partitions
Enable PITR in the table
Create a LSI to absorb the writing
questions.explanation: A) Correct: High cardinality key distributes traffic evenly between partitions — structural correction. B) Incorrect: larger items consume MAIS ability, aggravating the limit. C) Correct: when the natural key is of low cardinality, write sharding with suffix spreads the writings of the same logical value between N partitions. D) Incorrect: PITR it is data recovery, without relation to throughput. E) Incorrect: LSIs share the partition capacity of the table — do not absorb hot partitions.

questions.text: An organization with dozens of accounts in AWS Organizations needs three corporate guarantees: prevent the use of unapproved regions, audit calls from API in all accounts and continuously evaluate the conformity of resource configurations in all accounts. What three mechanisms implement these guarantees? (Select THREE Alternatives))
options: Service Control Policies (SCPs) with regional condition applied to OWs
IAM Same policies manually copied for each account
An organization trail of CloudTrail covering all member accounts
Amazon GuardDuty as a record of audit of API
AWS Config with organizational aggregator and conformance packs in accounts
Disable the creation of new accounts
questions.explanation: A) Correction: SCPs define the organisation's permission ceiling — the condition aws:RequestedRegion block Unapproved regions in TODAS the identity of the member accounts. B) Incorrect: manual copy is not governance — drifts and does not limit local admins. C) Correct: the organization trail records calls from API of all accounts at a central point. D) Incorrect: GuardDuty DETECTA threats using logs; who registers the audit is the CloudTrail. E) Correct: Config continuously evaluates the conformity of configurations, with aggregate view of the organization. F) Incorrect: preventing new accounts is not a compliance check.

questions.text: A cluster Amazon EMR executes batch processing in night with flexible time. The team wants to drastically reduce the cost of computing, accepting occasional interruptions of us SEM lose data from HDFS. Which ones DUAS Do practices achieve this safely? (Select DUAS alternatives)
options: Use instances Spot in the knot TASK (not stored HDFS), keeping primary and core in On-Demand
Use instances Spot in TODOS the knots, including the primary
Adopt transient clusters: create the cluster for the job (data no S3 way EMRFS) and shut it down at the end
Keep the cluster on 24/7 to avoid bootstrap time
Fold the size of the core knots
questions.explanation: A) Correct: we task only process — if Spot is taken, or YARN Reexecutes tasks in another node; core and primary are protected in On-Demand. B) Incorrect: lose primary in Spot drops the entire cluster; core in Spot risk data from HDFS. C) Correct: with data on S3 (EMRFS), the cluster becomes disposable: you only pay for the hours of the job. D) Incorrect: cluster 24/7 for night work is the waste that you want to eliminate. E) Incorrect: we increase the cost — the opposite of the objective.

questions.text: Financial records recorded in S3 shall, by regulation, remain immutable by 7 years: neither administrators nor root user can alter or exclude them during retention. DUAS configurations implement this requirement WORM? (Select DUAS alternatives)
options: Enable S3 Object Lock in mode COMPLIANCE with retention period of 7 years
Enable S3 Object Lock in mode GOVERNANCE, which prevents changes even by root
Enable Bucket Version (Object Lock pre-requirement))
Apply a bucket policy denying s3:DeleteObject, which cannot be reversed
Use SSE-KMS, which makes objects immutable
questions.explanation: A) Correct: compliance mode prevents exclusion/alteration by QUALQUER user, including root, until the end of retention — the WORM B) Incorrect: in governance mode, users with special permissions (s3:BypassGovernmentRetention) PODEM C) Correct: Object Lock requires enabled versioning in the pocket — both walk together. D) Incorrect: Bucket policies can always be changed by those who have permission (including root) — is not real immutability. E) Incorrect: encryption protects confidentiality, does not prevent exclusion.

questions.text: One API serverless (API Gateway + Lambda + DynamoDB) has high latency in the first accesses after idle periods and degradation in repeated readings of DynamoDB at peak times. DUAS Do optimizations attack the two problems, respectively? (Select DUAS alternatives)
options: Configure Provided Competition in function Lambda to remove cold starters
Increase function timeout Lambda
Reduce function memory to speed up startup
Add or DynamoDB Accelerator (DAX) as read cache in microseconds
Change to API HTTP by REST
questions.explanation: A) Correct: Provided Competition maintains pre-initialized run environments — the latency of the first access disappears. B) Incorrect: longer timeout only allows waiting longer; does not reduce latency. C) Incorrect: MENOS memory = less CPU = initialization and execution more LENTAS. D) Correct: or DAX is the native cache of DynamoDB — repeated readings begin to respond in microseconds, relieving the table in peaks. API does not resolve cold start or data cache.

questions.text: A company wants a real-time near-analysis pipeline with the MENOR operational effort: application events should reach S3 already in Parquet, be discovered/catalogated automatically and be immediately consultable in SQL. WHAT THREE services make up this serverless pipeline? (Select THREE Alternatives)
options: Amazon Kinesis Firehose data with native conversion to Parquet and destination S3
A self-managed Kafka cluster in EC2

Amazon EC2 with cron conversion jobs
Amazon Athena running the consultations SQL directly on the S3
Amazon Neptune to store events
questions.explanation: A) Correct: Firehose ingests, converts to Parquet and delivers no S3 no servers. B) Incorrect: Kafka in EC2 is the MAIOR possible operational effort for the same role. Glue discovers and maintains the catalogue (schemes/partitions) that the Athena use. D) Incorrect: EC2 + cron violates the serverless requirement and adds maintenance. Athena date or pipeline: SQL serverless direct at S3, F) Incorrect: Neptune is a graph bank — nothing to do with the scenario.

questions.text: A company connects its datacenter to AWS by a single link Direct Connect and suffered a total interruption when he failed. The requirement now is hybrid connectivity RESILIENTE, with an automatic and encrypted backup path if the DX fails again. DUAS do measures make up the solution? (Select DUAS alternatives)
options: Add a second connection Direct Connect in a different location (location)
Configure a Site-to-Site VPN online as a backup route of the Direct Connect, how to fail away BGP
Add more VIFs to the same link Direct Connect
Use VPC Peering as DX backup
Switch DX to Public Internet with Elastic IPs
questions.explanation: A) Correct: a second DX in distinct location eliminates the single point of physical failure — the most resilient option. B) Correct: a VPN Site-to-Site as backup gives an independent path (internet), encrypted, with automatic failure via BGP — the recommended design of balanced cost. C) Incorrect: more VIFs in MESMO link fall together with link. D) Incorrect: peering connects VPCs to each other — does not connect the datacenter. E) Incorrect: abandoning DX reduces the quality of connectivity instead of making it resilient.

questions.text: The invoice of a VPC revealed high cost of NAT Gateway: cases EC2 in private sub-networks transfer dozens of TB/month to the Amazon S3 and the DynamoDB through the NAT. Which ones DUAS changes eliminate this transfer cost while maintaining private access? (Select DUAS alternatives)
options: Create a Gateway VPC Endpoint for the S3 and adjust the route tables of private sub-networks

Move instances to public sub-networks
Compress the data before sending by NAT

B) Correct: or DynamoDB is the other service with free Gateway Endpoint — the same economy. C) Incorrect: more NATs divide traffic, but the collection by processed GB remains the same (or greater, by overtime). D) Incorrect: expose the instances publicly exchange cost for security risk. E) Incorrect: compression reduces the volume a little bit, but keeps the architecture expensive — the endpoints zero this cost..
